When he finally came close and began removing the chains, she made a helpless little sound against the gag because she had not realized until then how reluctant she was to leave the state.
Henry’s hand rested briefly at the back of her hood.
“Easy,” he said. “Come back slowly.”
He freed the chain, then the hood, then the gag. Cold air returned first. Light second. Selfhood in ragged pieces after that.
Sonia blinked at him, wrapped in a blanket before she had fully noticed him reaching for it. He sat with her on a low stone step just outside the villa where the last light was fading over the lake. She leaned into him without asking whether she should.
No theory came to help her.
Only the blunt fact that she had let Henry take control of her body, her face, her mouth, her movement, her stillness, and had come out of it not diminished but steadied.
“You stayed with me well,” he said.
The praise went through her like heat under the skin.
She closed her eyes.
“Sir,” she managed, because anything longer would have broken.
They loaded the equipment in near-darkness. Henry did most of the lifting. Sonia folded fabric, packed smaller pieces, checked the cases when he told her what went where. Simple tasks. Good tasks. On the drive back down the mountain she sat angled toward the window and watched Geneva gather itself out of evening shadow while another part of her replayed the moment the self had thinned and relief had rushed in behind it.
She had wanted the photographs to turn out well.
She had not expected the day to show her how much peace could live inside chosen helplessness.

title: Chapter 31: Exploring London
Chapter 32: Maid Service
Chapter 33: The Eden Nexus
content:
The Eden Nexus# The Eden Nexus sat downriver in a stretch of transformed landscape so deliberate it looked almost fictional from the train.
Domes rose from former industrial ground with a confidence Anna found immediately appealing: environmental engineering made visible, but not ugly, and every structure carrying the same British instinct she had already begun to recognize elsewhere. Nothing merely existed. Everything managed something.
Julien seemed pleased by her eagerness.
He had dressed her in one of the teal catsuits under a Victorian blouse, latex stockings, and an inflated skirt restrictive enough to keep her pace short without making a day trip impossible. Her hands were locked into the muff again. A hat with layered veils softened her face without muting her completely. The rail attachment at her corset kept her beside him in a calm line of dependence she now found more soothing than embarrassing.
Their guide introduced herself as Jonathan Vane’s Eleanor.
Anna’s first reaction was confusion so sharp it nearly became offense.
Eleanor looked more exposed than any respectable woman in Geneva ever would have, even though her outfit was plainly functional rather than provocative. Heavy protective latex still streaked with mud. Practical platform boots. A broad collar. An integrated corset line. The visible maintenance adapter of her chastity belt under the suit. Her face hidden by a hood made for field conditions, not prettiness. She looked like someone the weather and the work had been allowed to touch directly.
Anna, arranged in careful British elegance at Julien’s side, felt both superior and immediately defensive.
Eleanor did not appear to notice.
“Mr. Moreau,” she said. “And this must be Anna.”
Julien made the introductions. Anna answered with a polite greeting through her veil.
“Good,” Eleanor said. “That will save time.”
The remark should have charmed Anna.
Instead it unsettled her. Eleanor moved through the place with the loose authority of a woman whose usefulness had made certain concessions possible. She was obviously restrained, but according to a logic different from Anna’s own, not less dependent so much as dependent elsewhere.
Eleanor led them through biome domes that recreated climates and managed transitions with technical confidence: fog capture, rainwater systems, thermal layering, preserved habitats, invasive newcomers, pre-collapse landscapes held in careful simulation beside their altered descendants. Julien was genuinely interested. Anna was too, but she kept finding her attention pulled sideways toward Eleanor.
She watched how Julien listened to her. She watched how easily old familiarity moved between them. She watched Eleanor stride where Anna had to glide.
The jealousy started there, quietly.
It was not a simple fear of losing Julien to Eleanor. Eleanor represented a kind of female usefulness Anna did not possess, one that seemed to earn freedom of movement, practical clothing, open competence, conversational equality. Anna, clipped to Julien and prettied into dependence, suddenly felt ornamental in a way that stung.
Eleanor was explaining one of the colder domes when Julien laughed at something from an older field story. Eleanor laughed too, and for a second they were visibly people who had once known each other before Anna existed in this arrangement at all.
The feeling in Anna’s chest sharpened.
Her hands were shut away in the muff. She could not break into the conversation gracefully, and even turning toward Julien required permission from the rail and skirt. The whole outfit that had pleased her so much an hour earlier now seemed built to remind her of her place.
That was, of course, because it was.
She hated how much the thought steadied her.
When they stopped in the administration building so Eleanor could clean up after field work, Julien unhitched Anna from the outdoor rail and adjusted the attachment for indoor range. The freedom was relative, but enough. Eleanor disappeared into the women’s service area and reappeared a moment later holding out a hose with matter-of-fact confidence.
“Would you mind?”
Anna took it at once.
Helping another woman undress for maintenance should have felt intimate in a way she would need to think about later. In the moment it mostly felt practical. She rinsed mud from the latex while Eleanor stood with her arms slightly out from her sides and the water sheeted down over the dark material. The suit was engineered for labor, and the labor had marked it openly.
When Eleanor peeled back the hood, Anna saw a face almost shockingly bare: no painted softness, no ornamental veil, no effort spent on prettiness beyond simple care. For a second Anna felt almost embarrassed by the amount of time she herself spent being arranged.
That feeling did not survive what came next.
Eleanor stepped into the maintenance booth to attach the evacuation adapter to her chastity belt with the same resigned ease Anna used when lifting her veils to eat in public. The process was not decorative and did not attempt to be. Foot clamps. Wrist grips. The adapter rising between her feet to meet the exposed fitting of the belt. Cleaning, emptying, rinsing, reset. Everything done by system. Everything efficient. Everything beyond her control for the duration.
Anna watched with something like fascination.
Eleanor, noticing, gave the smallest shrug available under the mechanism.
“Field day,” she said. “Best not to romanticize the practicals.”
Anna lowered her gaze briefly in acknowledgment.
“I was not mocking.”
“I know.”
When Eleanor emerged and began dressing for the administrative part of the day, the earlier contrast clarified itself. She did not become less controlled when she changed. She became differently controlled. Blouse. Latex skirt. Bonnet. Veils. Public composure layered over the hidden mechanical necessities of a working ward whose body had to be managed for reasons Anna herself did not share.
It struck Anna then that jealousy had been too simple a word for what she felt.
Eleanor’s life contained ugliness Anna would not have wanted. Anna’s life contained ornamental dependence Eleanor clearly did not receive. Neither of them was free. Both of them were cherished in ways shaped by use.
That last thought startled her.
She said it quietly while fastening the last of the outer buttons for her:
“You work very hard.”
Eleanor’s eyes flicked to hers.
“So do you.”
Anna almost denied it. Then she stopped.
Because from Eleanor’s point of view the answer was probably obvious. The clothes. The rail. The muff. The posture. The effort of being beautiful in the approved way all day long. That too was labor, only in another register.
“Differently.”
“Yes,” Eleanor said. “Differently.”
That was the moment the jealousy began to loosen.
It did not loosen into friendship, not yet, but into recognition.
By the time they returned to Julien, Anna no longer felt diminished by Eleanor’s practicality. She had glimpsed another branch of the same order: another way a woman could be bound, maintained, and valued inside it.
Julien looked between them and saw enough to ask no foolish questions.
“All well?”
Anna answered with deliberate clarity.
“Yes, Sir. Thank you for bringing me.”
He watched her face.
“You mean that.”
“Yes, Sir.”
And she did. The day had shown her something useful about the world being larger than the small vanity of imagining her own restrictions the only meaningful kind. Her life was not better than Eleanor’s or worse, only shaped for another use. Walking back through the Nexus at Julien’s side, rail lightly guiding her and muff warm at her waist, Anna felt lighter for having understood that.

title: Chapter 34: Trial Maid
content:
Trial Maid# The week after Sonia’s night in the maid dress stretched and tightened around her at once.
Work continued. Meetings, data, polite evasions, careful clothes. She functioned. She was even good at functioning. But something in her had turned toward Henry and stayed there. By Wednesday, keeping that turn private had begun to feel less like dignity than delay.
They met again at Les Petits Chats after work.
Sonia arrived in a cream dress with a wide skirt, a fitted jacket, gloves, and the lace mask Henry already knew. The Yoyah Sheengzoh under the skirt kept her steps short enough that the approach to his table felt like a small performance of discipline. She did not mind that. She had stopped pretending she disliked being looked at by him when she was dressed correctly.
Henry stood as she approached, took in the outfit, and seated her.
“You look impeccable,” he said.
Thank you, Sir.
The praise calmed her enough to let her speak plainly.
I would like to propose something.
He glanced at her hands, then back to her face.
“Go on.”
Anna away for some time still. My evenings are my own. If it suits you, I would like to spend part of that time in your service as a trial for a few weeks. I would come to your house, live there properly, and see whether this can hold outside exceptional days.
Henry did not answer at once.
That was wise. The proposition deserved the weight of a real pause.
“You mean as my maid.”
Yes, Sir.
“And more than that.”
Sonia lowered her eyes.
Yes, Sir.
He sat back, considering her with an attention that made the café around them feel thinner.
“Why now?”
Because I am already half there. Because going home to my own apartment feels increasingly like being sent away from the life I want. Because I liked sleeping at your feet more than I have liked most conventional attempts at intimacy in my adult life.
She did not say any of those first.
Because I would rather test this honestly than keep circling from safe distance, she signed. Then, after a beat, more quietly: And because I miss it.
That answer pleased him enough that she could hear the change in his breathing.
“Good,” he said. “I was wondering how long you intended to wait before admitting that.”
Sonia felt heat move through her and let it. He was right.
“If we do this,” Henry continued, “it will not be decorative. You will be under rules. You will be dressed for the role. I will expect obedience the first time. I will also expect you to speak when something is wrong during it, not after.”
Yes, Sir.
“And if I decide you need more structure than a dress and a schedule can provide?”
She knew what he meant before he said it.
Then I will listen, Sir.
“You will do more than listen.”
The sentence sent a pulse low through her body.
Yes, Sir.
He nodded once.
“All right. A trial.”
Relief hit so cleanly she had to hide it by reaching for her coffee.
“There is one condition,” he said.
She looked up.
“For the duration, I want certainty about our boundaries. You and I will not improvise past them because desire is convenient. I have had a belt made for you.”
Sonia’s fingers tightened on the cup.
A belt.
“Yes.”
He held her gaze while the meaning settled.
“You may still refuse the arrangement.”
She could.
That remained important.
It also remained less appealing than the thought of accepting.
The belt was not simply denial. She understood that at once. It was structure. It was him taking responsibility for the edges of something she already wanted badly enough to distrust herself with it.
Permanent?
“Not beyond the trial unless we decide so together.”
And during trial?
“During the trial it will come off when I decide it should.”
Her mouth went dry behind the mask.
Yes, Sir, she signed.
Henry watched her closely.
“You mean that.”
Yes.
“Good.”
They settled the practicalities after that. She would come that evening. He would provide most of what she needed. She could bring the Shanghai maid uniform because he understood it mattered symbolically. He said the word symbolically with enough precision that she knew he also understood the symbolism had become flesh.
By the time Sonia stood at the door of his villa later that night with her suitcase beside her, she was too deep in the decision to call it nerves. It felt more like a controlled fall.
Henry opened the door before she rang a second time.
She curtsied.
Your maid has arrived, Sir.
“Come in.”
No flourishes. No joke to soften it.
The directness steadied her.
He took the suitcase and led her through the house slowly, not as a tour but as orientation. Study. Kitchen. Laundry. The small maid room beside his own room. Storage. Service stair. Bell pull. Rail points at certain thresholds, less common than in London but present where they would matter. He showed her where things belonged and how he expected the house to look at the end of an evening.
“You can change now,” he said when they reached the maid room. “When you are ready, come to the study.”
The room was narrow and orderly, not cruelly sparse, only specific. Bed, wardrobe, mirror, a chair, drawers for things she would need to keep in place. It should have felt diminishing. Sonia set the suitcase down and felt instead a strange, shameful surge of relief. No ambiguity. No decorative femininity without function. A room for a woman whose role had been decided.
She changed into the maid uniform carefully, taking more time than she needed because the ritual itself mattered. When she stepped into the study afterward, Henry was at his desk with a key ring and a flat white box laid out before him.
She curtsied.
“Your maid is ready, Sir.”
“Come here.”
She crossed the room. He walked around her once, inspecting the uniform, the collar, the gloves, the line of the apron, the state of her shoes. Nothing in the examination was lustless, but neither was it random. He was checking her as something entrusted to him.
“You look right,” he said.
That approval made her stand straighter.
Then his tone shifted.
“Now we fit the belt.”
He opened the box.
Sonia had imagined it already and still felt her stomach turn when she saw it. White composite, shaped exactly for her body, clean enough to look clinical and intimate enough to make that clinical quality obscene. He let her look. He did not rush her past it.
“You may still say no.”
There was the exit again.
She hated him a little for leaving it there because refusing remained technically possible and therefore acceptance had to remain hers.
“No,” she said. “I want it.”
His eyes held hers for a moment, then dropped briefly in acknowledgment.
“Undress from the waist down.”
She obeyed.
The fitting was methodical. Corset first, because the belt would lock into it. Then the belt itself, fitted up beneath, aligned, checked, adjusted. Henry worked with concentration, not theatricality. The restraint did not become hotter by being treated as a toy. It became hotter by being treated as infrastructure, something serious enough to deserve exact hands and a man who intended to be responsible for it.
When the last fittings clicked into place against the corset hardware, Sonia felt the reality of it travel through her body in stages. Coolness. Pressure. Foreignness. Then the worst part: immediate comprehension.
She was accessible only by his decision now.
The knowledge made her flush so hard she had to grip the edge of the dressing table.
Henry noticed.
“Too much?”
“No, Sir.”
It was not too much. It was almost too right.
He touched the side of her waist lightly where the corset and belt met.
“Walk.”
She walked the length of the room and back. Different. Definite. The belt changed not only what she could do, but how every step reported itself to her. Presence at the center of her body. Closedness. Supervision.
“And?”
Sonia stopped before him.
“I can feel it all the time.”
“That is the point.”
Yes. It was.
He dressed her again afterward, not fully, only enough to settle her back into the uniform. By then her thoughts had become oddly simple, not empty but ordered.
Henry showed her where the maid room key hung, what time breakfast would be, what to call him in the house, and where she would place things once unpacked. He did not push her into a scene. He did something more dangerous. He treated the arrangement as already real.
Later, alone in the maid room, Sonia sat on the edge of the narrow bed in stays, stockings, and uniform pieces not yet fully unfastened and put a hand over the front of the corset where the belt locked in beneath it.
The barrier answered with silence.
She lay down eventually, then rose again, then lay down once more. The bed was fine. The room was fine. Her body was not distressed. It was alert. Kept. Every shift of her hips reminded her that she had handed the center of her sexual access to Henry and had done so voluntarily.
The thought should have felt like defeat.
Instead it felt like the end of argument.
The fear had not vanished. She was afraid of the discipline, of correction, of the speed with which peace kept appearing inside structures she had once dismissed as degrading. She was afraid too of how easily the word his had started to form in her mind.
But lying there in the little maid room beside Henry’s bedroom, locked and held and no longer required to negotiate with herself about what she wanted, Sonia felt something open instead of close.
She had not become less herself.
She had become easier to inhabit.
Sometime after midnight, with one hand resting over the corseted line of her stomach and the other tucked under her cheek, Sonia finally slept with the calm knowledge that the trial had already begun to answer its own question.
She could belong to him.
And she wanted to be his.

title: Chapter 35: Reunion in the Garden
content:
Reunion in the Garden# Three years after the Change, Sonia had been Henry Serrurier’s Sonia for quite a while now.
Walking through Geneva’s community garden, she admired the lush surroundings. This place, once part of the concrete wasteland of Geneva airport, was now a thriving green space. Every path and planting bed showed careful attention, order, beauty, and purpose forced into the same shape.
She noticed a group of young women approaching in the distance. They moved in perfect synchronization, marching in a precise double row. They were students from the École de Réforme du Nord-Ouest, a reformatory school in the northwest quarter of the city, near the former airport. The school was for young women who struggled to adjust to their Change.
The students wore immaculate uniforms: modest blouses with high collars, gray blazers, and ankle-length skirts that swayed slightly with each step. Their faces were concealed behind identical porcelain masks, and their hair was hidden under neat headscarves. The overall effect was one of strict uniformity, their only visible distinction the name tags catching the sun.
When they reached a designated area in the garden, the group came to a precise halt. With military efficiency they shifted into a single line, standing at attention with perfect posture as they waited for instruction. Their teacher, an older woman whose uniform differed only in the color and stripes at the hem of her skirt, began her inspection. She moved methodically down the line, her sharp eyes catching every small deviation. A slight correction here, a minor adjustment there, and the students were once again flawless.
Satisfied, the teacher signaled for the next phase. The students quickly pulled on green gardening aprons in coordinated, fluid movements. Two women from the garden staff arrived, pushing rolling carts filled with neatly organized tools. The teacher gave a series of hand signs, directing the students into pairs and groups of four. Tools were distributed, and the young women turned to their tasks with disciplined precision.
Working in the garden gave them a small measure of autonomy inside a tightly controlled setting. Here, among the greenery, they found purpose and the chance to contribute while the school kept their behavior inside the strict bounds society expected.
Closer by, Sonia noticed a small graceful figure moving between the beds. The woman’s movements were precise, almost like a ballet dancer’s. She wore a bonnet over her hair, and the cut of her blouse suggested a tight corset underneath, emphasizing her slim waist. She wore a crisp white Gobao Yoohoo with a high collar together with an Edwardian walking skirt in deep navy blue, covered by a gardening apron in a slightly brighter shade. There was no rank insignia at all on the hem of her skirt.
Every step showed the limits imposed by her clothing. Her gloved hands moved with precision as she communicated with the others in the garden. The gloves were elegant yet sturdy, suitable for work. What little could be seen of her face beneath the bonnet was hidden behind a porcelain mask. That made her hard to identify, but the elegance of her movements felt familiar to Sonia.
Sonia watched the woman move through the beds and the work teams around them. She corrected one girl’s hand position on a tool handle, redirected another with a quick sign toward the greenhouse path, and had two men checking an irrigation plan within minutes without ever seeming to give an order. That ability to shape outcomes without visibly claiming them reminded Sonia of Mara’s strategic brilliance.
Mara Delacroix, once called Mara the Merciless, had been a corporate lawyer before the Change. She had helped Sonia identify key figures behind the virus. Then Sonia had gone to Shanghai, the world had lurched forward without either of them asking permission, and by the time she came back, Mara had vanished from the legal world.
After watching for a while, Sonia decided to approach. She took a breath, stepped forward, and tapped the woman’s shoulder. The woman turned, and though her face was masked, Sonia sensed recognition at once.
Mara? Sonia signed tentatively. It is Sonia. I was… Sonia Becker. She hesitated before signing her pre-Change name. Using it felt wrong. I am Henry Serrurier’s Sonia. Long time. You well?
Mara’s gloved hands paused, then answered with formal precision.
Henry Serrurier’s Sonia. I am Philippe Beaumont’s Mara.
Then her signing softened.
Good seeing you, Sonia. I am well. Thank you for asking.
Relief and joy lit up Sonia’s face, her smile visible in her eyes even behind her own mask.
Thought I recognized you. You have done amazing work here.
Mara’s hands moved again, fluid and precise.
Thank you. This garden is labor of love. I am glad you approve.
Sonia looked around, taking in the thriving greenery and the quiet sense of order.
It is beautiful. Truly. But how did you manage all this, after everything changed?
Mara’s hands moved with calm confidence.
It has been journey. Much changed, including me. But I found new ways to contribute. The garden reflects commitment to sustainability and community.
Sonia nodded.
Would like hear more. Maybe we walk and sign?
Mara tried to nod, found the motion difficult, and gave a shallow curtsy instead.
Would like that very much, Sonia. Much to share.
As they began to walk, Mara signed, After the Change, I found I could not continue legal career. And I needed find guardian.
She hesitated, and Sonia understood.
Sonia understood that pressure well enough herself, the constant scrutiny, the demand to conform, the way the world now kept asking women to become easier to manage.
Mara continued.
I found Philippe, and he took me as ward. He suggested I find project aligned with social values. Community garden came from that.
Sonia took that in.
What you have done here is amazing, Mara.
Mara’s signs became more formal again.
I only helped make it happen. Community did the work.
As they walked, a young woman in uniform approached, looking uncertain.
Madam Mara, she signed. Need help with compost area. New bins arrived, but not sure how set them up.
Mara responded immediately.
Of course. Get Camille. She knows setup and will teach you. I check later.
The young woman nodded and hurried off, visibly relieved.
As they kept walking, Mara resumed her story.
Garden also place for learning and rehabilitation. Young women come here when adjustment difficult. Work helps.
They paused beside a group of women tending a herb bed. Mara gently corrected one woman’s technique with a few precise signs. The woman’s gratitude was obvious.
Farther along, they came across two men in tailored suits, clearly important figures. Sonia stepped back at once, curtsied, and waited, as was expected of her.
“Madam Mara, if you have a moment?” Councillor Laurent said with quiet authority.
Mara curtsied and signed her greeting.
“We are discussing the garden expansion. There are concerns about funding and logistics.”
Mara’s eyes brightened behind her mask as she answered.
Councillor Laurent, appreciate your concerns. Might be able offer solution, if it suits planning. Minister Jacques Laborde provides National Sustainability Fund.
She produced a slim binder from within her skirts.
If you kindly check paperwork, will find prepared proposal for review. With your approval, it could go to ministry.
The other man, Councillor Dubois, looked interested.
“A National Sustainability Fund? That could solve our problems.”
Mara continued.
Yes, Sir. Proposal shows the garden meets fund goals, making it eligible for seventy-five percent funding. Securing grant would highlight your commitment to environmental initiatives.
Laurent took the proposal from her and glanced through it.
“This could indeed show our dedication to sustainability. We will review it thoroughly.”
Mara curtsied more deeply.
Thank you, Sirs. Here to support community any way I can.
As the men walked away, Sonia admired how smoothly Mara had handled them.
You manage them very well, Mara. Like orchestrating everything behind the scenes.
Mara answered with the same humble restraint.
Only offer guidance. True credit belongs to community.
As they walked on, Sonia could not shake her awe. Mara had adapted to Changed society and found a way to thrive. Her ability to influence and guide without visibly overstepping was remarkable. Yet it was clear that the Mara Sonia was speaking to was, in part, still a persona built for navigating society.
Even so, Sonia was deeply impressed, and more unsettled by that than she wanted to be.
Mara, you are amazing. Glad found you again.
Mara’s hands moved smoothly.
And glad you are here, Sonia. Together…
Her hands froze in mid-sign, and she made a muffled sound behind the mask. Then she stopped completely, a subtle tremor passing through her posture.
Need go, Mara signed quickly, her hands trembling slightly.
Sonia’s eyes widened with concern.
Mara, all right?
Mara signed back, her movements now smaller and more controlled.
Yes, Sonia. Brought this on myself. iGuardian switching discipline mode because I am late. She paused, then added, Please do not worry. Will be fine.
Sonia watched Mara glide away in short steps, her hard heels clicking rapidly on the paving slabs. Even in obvious discomfort, she held herself with poise that spoke of years of training and adaptation.
Understanding came to Sonia all at once. She had heard enough about the iGuardian to know what discipline mode implied, and what it meant that Mara was still moving with that much control while it was happening.
A young woman approached Sonia and curtsied.
Excuse me, Madam. Can help you with anything? Saw you with Madam Mara.
Sonia smiled and signed back.
Thank you, but I am fine. Madam Mara had attend something urgent. I was only admiring the work here.
The young woman nodded, pride visible even through her mask.
We all very dedicated to garden. Madam Mara’s guidance invaluable.
Sonia’s heart warmed.
It is truly impressive. Dedication and effort remarkable.
The young woman beamed with her eyes and excused herself.
Sonia drew a deep breath against the restriction of her corset and stood for a moment without moving. For all the strictness of Changed society, the garden held real energy. Mara had cultivated more than plants. She had cultivated a functioning world inside the larger one, and Sonia felt a dangerous flicker of wanting that world to make room for her too.
Meanwhile, Mara hurried through the garden paths. The iGuardian was relentless, driving her onward with painful impulses deep inside her and sharp corrective signals in her breast electrodes. The stiff collar of her neck corset, integrated with her mask and gag, prevented her from turning her head at all, forcing her to rely on a narrow field of vision.
Each step was a struggle against escalating correction, close to unbearable by then. She had only herself to blame. She knew better than to be late to Philippe. The reunion with Sonia had carried her away enough to make her lose track of time, and now the device was teaching the lesson back into her body. The mask restricted her breathing, the gag filled her mouth, and the electrodes kept up their punishing rhythm while she hurried on, graceful to anyone watching, suffering to the core.

title: Chapter 36: Three years earlier: The End of Delacroix and Partners
Chapter 37: Planning a charity ball
content:
Planning a charity ball# Back in the present, Mara reached the café where Philippe was waiting. It was a modern place with outdoor seating, and the specially shaped women’s chairs were clearly visible. Her belt’s corrections stopped as soon as she came close enough for Philippe’s phone to pick up her iGuardian’s signature. Mara curtsied in greeting, her body trembling slightly from the exertion and the corrections. Philippe stood to greet her with a smile.
He did not mention her lateness. The iGuardian had already delivered the necessary correction. His phone had notified him when it began, but he had chosen to leave it in discipline mode a while longer. It would keep Mara silent and exact, correcting even the smallest deviation from protocol. It would do her good to be reminded, from time to time, of the expected behavior.
He rose and motioned for her to sit opposite him, making sure she had a clear view of him. As Mara sat, the back of her corset locked into the matching braces of the women’s chair, securing her in place. At Philippe’s gesture, a waitress approached and connected a feed bag to the adapter on Mara’s mask so she could receive nourishment.
Philippe’s meal arrived shortly afterward, and he began to eat. He glanced at Mara with warm attentive eyes.
“We need to discuss the upcoming charity ball,” he said, his tone both businesslike and affectionate. “It is the annual Green Gala, raising funds for the Ecological Preservation Fund.”
Mara signed her reply.
Yes, Sir. I have been coordinating with organizing committee. We secured several important guests, including national and international celebrities. She added, Theme this year is Nature’s Elegance, pointing to ecological awareness.
Philippe nodded, pleased.
“Good. Who are the key attendees?”
Mara signed, We have confirmations from Sir William Lemieux’s Helena, the well-known environmental scientist, and Lord Hargreaves, the philanthropist, with his ward Caroline. Internationally, we secured Tom Holland and his ward Zendaya. Their presence will draw significant media attention.
Philippe smiled.
“Excellent work, Mara. These guests will help ensure the event’s success. Is there anyone else we should consider?”
Mara hesitated briefly before signing.
Met old acquaintance today, Henry Serrurier’s Sonia from GAIA. She specializes in viral diseases. Given ecological focus, her expertise could be relevant. Might be beneficial include her guardian and her on guest list.
Philippe considered that.
“Extend an invitation to Henry Serrurier and his ward. Your judgment has proven reliable.”
He glanced at her feed bag, noting how low it was getting. He knew Mara needed to gain a little weight, but he also knew the constraints of her corset required small, frequent feedings.
As the bag neared empty, he signaled the waitress.
“Please disconnect the feed bag and clean the adapter.”
The waitress complied, detaching the bag and wiping the adapter clean. Mara remained motionless, posture perfect, eyes fixed on Philippe.
He resumed the conversation.
“I am glad you met Sonia again. Connections like hers are valuable. Make sure she feels welcomed and appreciated. Your network is a great asset, Mara.”
Mara’s hands moved in fluid hand-dancing.
Thank you, Sir. I will make sure Henry Serrurier and his ward receive proper invitation. Grateful for your trust and support.
Philippe’s smile softened, and he touched her gloved hand gently.
“You have earned it, Mara. Continue to do so, and we will achieve great things together.”
As always, when Philippe praised her, a wave of arousal moved through her. She relaxed into her corset, closed her eyes behind the mask, and let herself enjoy the feeling.
When they were both finished, Philippe asked for the bill, paid it, and rose. He took out a ward handle, a small grip he could attach to control Mara more directly. He released her from the chair and helped her to her feet, then clicked the handle into the connector at the small of her back. She moved in small careful steps, her skirt and boots allowing little else.
“Let us go,” he said softly, guiding her by the handle at her back and indicating the exit.
Outside, he signaled for an electric cab. The driver hurried over and opened the door while Philippe disconnected the handle. He helped Mara inside, guiding her to kneel on the fempad’s cushion with her back toward the front. He clicked her corset adapter into the fempad’s locking arms, which gently drew her back into the padded supports. Once she was secure, Philippe sat down opposite her.
As the cab pulled away, Philippe held Mara’s gloved hand, a small gesture of comfort. She could not look up or turn her head, her vision too limited, but she felt his presence, steady and reassuring amid all her constraints, a silent promise of care.
The ride was short. Soon they arrived at Philippe’s villa in Cologny. The driver opened the door, Philippe stepped out first, then turned back to help Mara. He unlocked her from the fempad, helped her stand, and guided her out of the cab, again attaching the handle to her back.
“Almost home,” Philippe murmured as he led her toward the villa entrance.
Inside, he removed the handle and tapped master bedroom on the LCD panel by the door. Mara’s iGuardian answered with a soft beep, and she felt the guidance impulses direct her toward the bedroom. Philippe adjusted the pace to suit her limited stride.
Mara had no choice but to follow where the system led. With discipline mode still active, she took extra care not to trigger any further correction. The soft pulses of the guidance system were a constant reminder of how little control she had.
In the bedroom, the system guided her into a corner and then stopped. She stood there perfectly still, breathing shallowly through mask and gag. The room was quiet except for the faint rustle of her clothes as she shifted, trying to find some comfort within her rigid constraints.
Her mind began to drift, and she found a strange peace in the simplicity of obedience. In moments like this she felt relief from the constant demands of her strategic mind. Here she did not have to think or plan. She only had to follow. Philippe’s presence, and his care, gave her a comforting sense of security. The pulses guiding her reminded her that she was safe. She was secure.
A few minutes later Philippe entered the room, his expression softer.
“You did well today,” he said quietly, triggering the conditioned reward response that all Changed women carried.
A quick tap on his phone and an acknowledgement beep from the iGuardian released her from the position the system had assigned.
He led her to the bed.
“Now let us get you ready for the night.”
Mara curtsied and signed a formal acknowledgment.
Thank you, Sir. I am ready.
Philippe began preparing her for the night with his usual care. First he unlocked her bonnet and set it aside, leaving the mask in place. Then he released the central clothing lock at the small of her back, the key clicking softly. He opened her walking skirt and its support and helped her step out of it, revealing the tight underskirt underneath.
Next he released the stiff button panel of her blouse, sliding it free of the central lock. He shifted the two metal strips that held the back button row in place. Once the blouse could be opened, he worked his way down it methodically, easing each button through the aligned openings. Then he undid the cuffs and removed the blouse entirely so he could continue with her Yoyah Sheengzoh. He unlocked it and helped her out of it, leaving her standing in the iGuardian corset alone.
Her stockings were attached directly to the corset, and her feet were enclosed in knee-high ballet boots. The boots forced her into small steps and raised her a full twenty centimeters, bringing her small frame to a height more convenient for Philippe. Her hands were covered by full-length leather gloves suspended from the shoulder braces of the iGuardian, completing the ensemble that enforced an impeccable posture, a regal head position, and strict discipline.
Philippe led Mara to the bathroom and the cleaning station. He guided her boots into the ankle-loop locks that held her feet about a meter apart, then attached the cleaning adapter to the connector at the back of her iGuardian. Finally he raised her gloved hands to the shoulder-height arm locks at the sides. Held fully in place, she could do nothing but wait as the cleaning cycle began.
The cleaning adapter read the device configuration. It began filling her with an enema. The integrated catheter released, allowing her bladder to empty. The system started a mild reward program to make the wait more bearable until the enema could be released.
When it was, the system increased the reward level, massaging and stimulating her more and more, but always stopping just short of release. It always did.
At last the locks disengaged, and Philippe supported her gently as he led her back to the bed. He instructed her softly to kneel and offered her a hand to hold. Mara obeyed.
He began undoing her hair, which had been tightly braided and rolled into a bun. With great care he released the braid, letting her hair fall over her shoulders. Then he brushed it in long tender strokes. The intimacy of the moment wrapped around them, a sharp contrast to the disciplined exterior he otherwise maintained. Once her hair was brushed through, he braided it again, this time loosely for sleep, and placed a gentle kiss on her head.
Then he raised her, guided her into the bed, put her legs into the sleep shackles, arranged her braid so she would not lie on it, and attached a tether from the top of the bed to the connector between her shoulder blades, a restraint and charging cable at once. He tightened the tether carefully, enough for her to feel the restriction without discomfort.
“Mara,” Philippe said softly, his voice carrying both affection and authority, “you did very well today. Rest now. Tomorrow we have much to plan for the Green Gala.”
Mara signed back.
Thank you, Sir. I will rest and be ready for tomorrow.
He guided her hands into their shackles, locked them together, and attached them to the slot at the front of her corset with a short leash. Then he used his phone to loosen the collar, braces, and corset slightly for more comfortable sleep. Finally he set the device to watch mode and disengaged discipline mode. She would be helpless, but the iGuardian would alert him to any problem.
Philippe smiled and laid a gentle hand on her shoulder before switching off the main light and leaving only a soft glow in the room. Mara, still masked, gagged, gloved, with her bound feet held en pointe in her boots and her arms secured to the front of the corset, fell asleep almost at once. She felt properly secured, and she knew Philippe would care for her.
Mara woke with the first light of dawn filtering through the curtains. She lay still against Philippe’s warm body beside her, feeling his arm draped over her titanium-clad waist.
He stirred, his hand moving to caress her. He touched the smooth porcelain of her mask and the few bare patches of skin available to him, making Mara shiver with pleasure. She savored it and pulled ever so slightly against her restraints, enjoying the helplessness of being held in place.
After a few moments Philippe released her shackled arms, the tether between her shoulder blades, and finally her legs. He guided her through her morning routine. The iGuardian took care of her needs without requiring any release from its restrictions, cleaning her inside and out before applying its programmed skincare cycle.
When that was done, Philippe led her back to the bed and lifted her gently until she was on her hands and knees. He inserted the key into the iGuardian, carefully removed her vaginal shield and the insert, and left her exposed to the cool air for the first time in more than a week. With one hand on her hips, she felt the other begin to play with her, exploring the wetness that rose in her almost immediately. Long denial had made her ready for him within seconds.
Then he caught her corset-clad hips with both hands and took her hard and quickly. Mara knew from experience that this would be one of their brief rough morning affairs. As his thrusts deepened, she bit down on the gag. When he commanded her to come, she did at once, rough use and conditioning joining together to push her over the edge. She purred into the gag, her hands gave way, and she collapsed forward onto the mask, driving the gag deeper into her mouth. Her own hot breath filled the inside of the mask, and for a moment she struggled for air. His hands still held her hips high and him deep inside her. Then they moved upward to her waist and her rigid covered breasts, drawing her upright again. With him still inside her, his arms around her waist, he whispered praise into her ear. She desperately wanted to lean back into him and cuddle, but the rigidity of the outfit made that impossible. At last he withdrew, slid the shield back into place, and guided her to the bathroom for another cleaning cycle she knew she would need.
Afterward, Philippe helped her detach the mask so she could brush her teeth, leaving the used one for cleaning and giving her today’s mask instead. It was a plain white Jinshuwan that covered only her mouth and nose but included her usual feed adapter and gag. When she had finished brushing, she pushed the gag into place. The high stiff collar of the iGuardian made it awkward for her to open wide enough to let the front shield slide in smoothly. Then she clicked the lower part of the Jinshuwan into the collar, locking the mask and its gag into an ensemble that once again forced her head into a fixed, immovable position.
In the bedroom, Philippe waited to dress her for the day. He changed her shoes, gloves, and stockings for fresh ones and chose a different underskirt, then locked the collapsible framework of a bustle over it. Once the cleaning cycle and base layer of her dress were complete, he tightened the iGuardian’s collar, braces, and corset to their daytime settings.
He selected a dress even more Victorian in spirit than the one she had worn the day before, a rich verdant silk embroidered with dark green vines climbing over the skirts and bodice, the pattern designed to emphasize her slender figure and narrow waist. After helping her into the skirt and arranging it over the bustle, he dressed her in the bodice. He threaded her arms into the narrow sleeves, pulled the bodice into place in front, and arranged the high collar. Then he closed the buttons at her cuffs and down her back, locking everything into place.
Philippe loosened Mara’s hair, quickly straightened it, then braided it tightly into a strict daytime braid before rolling it into a bun. He chose a poke bonnet and secured it with a clasp around the bun. The bonnet had a wide silk band that went under her chin, crossed, and wrapped around her neck. He tied it into a neat bow that draped down the back of her dress and fixed it with a locking pin. The long poke of the bonnet would make the day more difficult, especially with the collar and mask already preventing any turn of the head, but it ensured proper face modesty even with only a Jinshuwan.
Once she was fully dressed, Philippe stepped back to admire the result.
“You look perfect, Mara. Now let us go downstairs for breakfast. We have much to do today.”
He tapped the control panel, and she felt the guidance pulses activate, directing her down to the dining room. When she arrived, the pulses guided her to her chair and stopped only once she was seated and locked into the chair’s corset adapters. As usual, Philippe personally attached the feed bag to her adapter while the maid served his breakfast. Mara felt the feed gag fill her mouth, swelling gradually until it collapsed and forced her to swallow. After years of the routine, she had grown used to the sensations.
As Philippe began his breakfast, he turned his attention to Mara, ready to discuss the day.
“Today you will work in the community garden until around two,” he said. “I will come to pick you up, and then we will review the location for the Green Gala.”
Mara answered in gloved hand-dancing.
Yes, Sir. I planned several activities for garden today, including planting new sections and coordinating with volunteers.
Philippe nodded approvingly.
“Good. It is important that the garden be well maintained. Now tell me more about the activities planned.”
Mara detailed them with precise signing.
We will plant native species to promote biodiversity. This is one of the restored sections after old runway was removed and toxins cleared from ground. Oil, fuel, and heavy-metal contamination was extremely high, but soil exchange and contaminant-extraction bacteria seem to have revived the ground. Also intend organize workshop for volunteers on sustainable gardening practices. One group is women with attitude problems; they will need close supervision when working outside later. Other volunteer groups will help install rainwater collection system, and we will improve watering gradually by converting it to direct-to-root drip irrigation.
Philippe smiled.
“Excellent. Your dedication to the garden is admirable. Now, about the Green Gala. We will visit the newly built Ecoville Hotel in Grand-Saconnex. It is not far from the garden,” he assured her.
“The hotel is designed around ecological principles and uses no concrete,” he continued. “Instead, it is constructed entirely from wood and other natural materials. The grand ballroom is ideal for our event, which makes it a suitable location. You will review the facilities and give me an assessment of their suitability.”
Mara signed her acknowledgment, since she could not nod.
I will make sure note any details or adjustments needed.
Philippe took a sip of coffee, watching her intently.
“Mara, your presence and your judgment are invaluable. Your ability to see details others miss is one of your greatest strengths.”
Warm pride moved through her at the words.
Thank you, Sir. I will do utmost to ensure everything perfect.
When he finished breakfast, Philippe stood and came around the table to where Mara sat. He gently detached the feed bag and unlocked her from the chair.
“Let us get you ready for the garden. You have a busy day ahead.”
He signaled the maid, who had stood silent and motionless by the entrance the entire time, to clear away the breakfast things.
Then he helped Mara to her feet and set her guidance for the main door. There he configured the iGuardian’s geofencing to allow her to proceed to the garden and move within it. Finally he opened the door for her.
“I will see you at two,” he said, his voice carrying that familiar note of affectionate authority. “Make sure everything runs smoothly.”
Mara curtsied and signed a quick response.
Yes, Sir. I will.
Again she felt guide mode activate. A prickling sensation from the electrodes buried beneath the domes that lifted and cradled her breasts told her which way to turn and go. The system would also remind her to stay on course with escalating corrections if she strayed or dawdled. It led her to the tram that would take her to the garden and instructed her to wait in line with the other unattended women. The iGuardian’s Bluetooth functions identified her to the tram and logged her in on her transport pass. Once she reached the garden, the iGuardian allowed her to move freely inside the geofence Philippe had set around it. It would also make sure she went through feed and waste-relief cycles at the booth at the times he had scheduled, while keeping him informed if it detected any resistant behavior that might require correction.
Mara’s day in the community garden was mostly routine. She oversaw the planting as planned, coordinated the volunteers, and gave her workshop. The structure of the day gave her a sense of calm and purpose.
Shortly before two, Mara felt the subtle signals from the iGuardian reminding her to prepare for Philippe’s arrival. Determined not to slip into discipline mode again, she made sure her appearance was immaculate, smoothing her skirt and adjusting her bonnet. She stood at attention in the marked waiting area by the entrance, perfectly poised when Philippe arrived.
“Ready to go, Mara?” Philippe asked with a warm smile.
She curtsied and signed.
Yes, Sir. Everything in order.
Philippe led her to the tram stop, and soon they were on their way to the Ecoville Hotel in Grand-Saconnex.
The Ecoville Hotel was an impressive sight, blending naturally into the parkland around it. The three-story building, constructed entirely from natural materials, radiated harmony with its surroundings. Wooden beams and large varioglass panels, dimmed slightly against the sun, allowed natural light to flood the interior, while green roofs and climbing plants provided both insulation and beauty.
At reception they were greeted by a female concierge whose waist was laced into an impressively narrow silhouette. She wore the service uniform used throughout the hotel, including the identical full-face mask worn by all the staff. It concealed her entire face except for her eyes and enforced both anonymity and silence. Her lower body could not be seen at all, as she appeared to be built into the reception desk, her waist locked into place so that she remained fixed there.
Welcome to Ecoville Hotel, she signed to Philippe.
“We are here to review the venue for the upcoming Green Gala,” Philippe replied.
The concierge’s hands moved, pointing to the decorative brass name plate fixed at the front of her collar.
Welcome, Sir. My name is Marguerite. We expected you.
She gave a signal to one side, and another woman appeared, released from a waiting lockbox. She was dressed identically and wore exactly the same mask, curtsying to Philippe. Marguerite introduced her as Fleur, again by pointing to the name plate that was the only visible difference between them.
Fleur is event manager for hotel. She will show you around and answer your questions, Marguerite signed.
Mara found herself thinking, with invisible amusement behind the mask, that perhaps every woman working there had been given a flower name.
Fleur took over, curtsying once more before guiding them onward.
Please follow me.
Philippe nodded, and they followed. As they walked, Mara took in the elegance of the building. Wood, natural fibers, living plants. The whole hotel seemed to breathe, embodying the ecological principles it advertised.
Fleur led them into the grand ballroom, a vast room with a high ceiling, full of plant life. The roof structure of exposed wooden beams gave it real grandeur. Large windows opened onto the surrounding park, filling the room with natural light. The floor was reclaimed wood polished to a warm glow, and the walls were lined with living plants that deepened the sense of being inside something cultivated rather than merely built.
Philippe turned to Mara.
“What do you think, Mara?”
Turning her whole body in mincing en-pointe steps to compensate for her restrictions, Mara surveyed the room. Then her hands moved in fluid evaluation.
Perfect, Sir. Ballroom captures essence of Green Gala. Beautiful and inspiring atmosphere for guests.
Philippe smiled with clear satisfaction.
“Excellent. Let us discuss the arrangements in detail.”
Mara began her inspection of the ballroom with a critical eye, noting every detail. She glided across the floor, her hobble skirt and ballet boots hidden beneath the bustle, while the rapid clicking of her heels echoed softly.
The ballroom opened onto a beautiful terrace leading into the surrounding park. The view was breathtaking, all greenery and careful landscaping. But Mara quickly identified a problem. Some stretches of the terrace had soft ground where women in heels and formal dress would struggle. She herself could not step into those areas in her present attire.
She signed the point to Fleur.
Need paving plates or wooden planks in these areas, fitted to style of event. Otherwise guests in heels will struggle.
Though Fleur’s mask revealed nothing, her body language showed attentive understanding. She signed agreement and made note of it.
Will ensure those adjustments made, Madam Mara.
Back inside the ballroom, Mara identified several places where tether bars or lockable women’s chairs should be installed. Some guests from more restrictive cultures would need proper means to secure their women while attending to other matters. It would be grossly impolite not to provide for that.
She signed the observation to Fleur.
Must ensure female guests are comfortable and secure while guardians mingle or attend bar.
Fleur noted that as well, her hands moving efficiently.
Understood, Madam Mara. We have proper equipment here. Only needs installation according to your specifications.
Mara then asked about the lighting. Fleur explained in fluid hand-dancing that the hotel used British bioengineered bioluminescent plants for its base lighting, creating a soft natural glow. An additional LED system was available for events that needed stronger illumination.
Bioluminescent plants delightful touch, Mara signed, genuinely intrigued. Guests will be impressed.
Also in garden, along all walkways, Fleur explained.
Satisfied with the lighting, Mara turned to the question of the stage. As she and Fleur discussed placement and design, Philippe drifted out into the park-like garden, leaving Mara to the planning.
Fleur explained that the ballroom had a modular stage system that could be assembled according to the event’s needs. Mara studied the plans and identified the best position for visibility and access.
Stage should go here, she signed, indicating the point that gave a clear view from every part of the room. Everybody must see speakers and performers clearly. More restrictive restraint stations should also be placed where women can still see stage.
Fleur nodded.
Can arrange that, Madam Mara. Will coordinate with staff to match your specifications.
At last Mara addressed another practical point.
Some guests will require nourishment through feed ports, she signed, indicating her own mask. Guardians prefer more controlled diet. Please ensure catering prepared with feed bags and suitable nutrition.
Fleur reassured her at once.
Increasingly popular trend. We are fully equipped. No need worry.
She pointed toward the outdoor breakfast area, barely visible through the greenery. Mara adjusted herself and the poke of her bonnet until she could see what Fleur meant. Nearly half the female guests seated there were already locked into women’s chairs with feed bags dangling from them.
Once the review was complete, Mara was satisfied. The venue was almost perfect, and with a few minor adjustments it would be ideal for the Green Gala. She was confident the event would succeed and reflect all the careful planning Philippe had allowed her to invest in it.
With the details noted and Fleur’s assurances in place, Mara joined Philippe outside in the garden. He was admiring the calm landscape when she approached, the soft rustle of her skirts announcing her.
Philippe turned with a smile.
“How does it look, Mara?”
Her hands moved with practiced grace.
Beautiful, Sir. Only few minor adjustments needed. It will be perfect for Green Gala.
Philippe nodded, clearly pleased.
“Excellent. Let us make sure everything is ready. This will be an event to remember.”

title: Chapter 38: Two years earlier: Fitting
content:
Two years earlier: Fitting# Mara had “earned” herself the iGuardian two years earlier and had lived in its unyielding titanium shell ever since.
As she drove back to the villa, her gloved hands gripped the steering wheel tightly. The meeting had gone well, or at least that was what she told herself. She had made her points, cut through the indecision, and ensured that things moved forward. But as the villa came into view, a knot of anxiety twisted in her stomach. She knew Philippe would not see it that way. She had not asked permission to attend the meeting, and she had not informed him at all. She had simply acted, driven by the same instinct that had always made her take control and make things happen.
Mara parked the car and took a deep breath, trying to calm herself before entering the house. Before getting out, she carefully worked the gag into her mouth and secured the porcelain mask over her face, slipping back into the role she was supposed to play. During the meeting, she had felt the need to speak, using both voice and hand-dancing together, something young girls often did before they received their first mask.
As soon as she stepped inside, she knew something was wrong. The house was too quiet. Philippe was waiting for her in the study, standing by the window with his back to the door. He knew, of course. He always did. She approached slowly, her heart pounding. As she entered the room, he turned to face her, his expression stern.
Without a word, Philippe gestured for her to stand in front of him. She complied, her posture as straight as she could make it. He did not speak at first. He simply watched her with those intense eyes that always seemed to see straight through her.
At last he broke the silence.
“You went to the meeting,” he said, his voice calm and cold.
Mara nodded, her hands moving quickly as she began to explain herself in hand-dancing. She tried to show that it had been necessary, that the situation had called for quick action, and that she had only been trying to help. Even while she signed, she knew it would not be enough.
Philippe watched her hands, then shook his head.
“You did not ask permission. You acted on your own. You removed your mask and used your voice, knowing perfectly well how unacceptable that is.”
Mara’s heart sank. She knew what was coming. She had crossed the line, and there would be no talking her way out of it. Not with him. She had broken the rules she had promised to follow. Again. And now she would face the consequences. Again.
Philippe stepped closer, his gaze fixed on hers.
“Do you understand why this is unacceptable?” he asked.
Mara hesitated, then nodded. Her hands moved more slowly this time.
I thought necessary. I thought helping.
Philippe’s expression softened, but only slightly.
“You need to learn that your actions have consequences, Mara. There are few rules. They are easy to follow. You need to ask for permission. Once it is given, you may do these things, properly, and in the required form. I know perfectly well that you understand form. It is no different from ballet.”
He moved to the desk and retrieved an armbinder, the leather gleaming darkly in the soft light. Mara’s breath caught in her throat as she realized what he intended. This was meant to remind her of her place, to keep her from acting out of turn again, to reinforce the boundaries she kept trying to push.
Philippe approached her, the armbinder in one hand.
“Turn around.”
Mara did as she was told, her heart pounding even harder now. She felt the leather slide up her arms, the straps pulled tight behind her back and over her shoulders. The armbinder was uncomfortable, completely restrictive.
Once it was secured, Philippe guided her over to a chair. He sat down and gestured.
“Bend over.”
Mara lowered herself over his knees, the position awkward with her arms bound. Philippe pulled up on her arms with one hand, and she tensed when she felt his other hand settle on her back, pressing her forward slightly. The spanking that followed was firm and controlled, but not gentle. Each strike carried the same clear message: she had gone too far.
Mara bit down on the gag, trying to hold back the sounds of pain and frustration that threatened to escape. She felt shame, anger, and also a strange sense of relief. She had known this would happen. She had known she would be corrected. In some twisted way, it felt right. She had disobeyed, and this was the price.
When it was over, Philippe stepped back and allowed her to straighten. He moved in front of her, his expression unreadable.
“You will remember this, Mara,” he said, his voice low. “You are to ask permission before taking any action like this again. You are to follow the rules I set for you. Do you understand?”
Mara nodded quickly, unable to speak and unable to sign.
Philippe watched her for another moment, then nodded.
“Good. You may go to your room now. The armbinder stays on until I say otherwise.”
Mara rose slowly, the discomfort of the armbinder making every movement difficult. She made her way to her room, her burning cheeks still carrying the correction she had just received. When she finally reached the bed, she sank onto the mattress, her mind racing.
She knew why it had happened. She knew she had been wrong to act without consulting Philippe, to remove her mask, to interrupt. But knowing it did not make acceptance any easier. She had always been someone who took the lead, someone who made things happen. Now she was being trained to submit, to follow instead of lead.
And the worst part was that she knew she would do it again. She could not seem to help it. It was who she was.
She was also a ballet dancer, and pain to her had always been part of the process, a necessary obstacle to overcome in the pursuit of perfection. It was temporary discomfort, something to work through the way she had worked through stretches and rehearsals.
But she also knew that Philippe was right. She could not keep acting like this, not if she wanted to stay with him, not if she wanted to avoid constant correction. The tension between her instincts and the rules was tearing her apart, and she did not know how much longer she could keep fighting it.
As she lay there with the armbinder tight against her skin, Mara realized that she needed to find some way to balance her old self with the new rules she was living under. If she did not, there would be more corrections, more pain, and more frustration.
A few days later, the villa fell into the kind of quiet morning that usually made Mara restless. Philippe had left early to attend to personal matters, leaving her alone with her thoughts and a household that seemed to move at a maddeningly slow pace. As she wandered through the rooms, she noticed small inefficiencies everywhere: disorganized files in Philippe’s office, staff moving about without clear direction, even a missed chance to secure a better deal with a supplier who had called earlier.
Mara’s instinct to take control rose before she could stop it. She had always been someone who saw what needed doing and did it, and today was no different. She began in Philippe’s office, rearranging the files and documents into a system that made more sense to her. Each folder found its place according to her own logic, a structure she believed would make it easier for Philippe to find what he needed. She worked quickly, focused on efficiency rather than the rules she was breaking.
Satisfied with the office, Mara turned to the household staff. Their routines looked disorganized, tasks scattered and badly sequenced. She started giving new instructions, reorganizing duties to create a smoother flow. The staff hesitated at first, clearly uncomfortable, but eventually followed her lead. They were used to taking orders from Philippe, but with him away, they obeyed Mara instead, uncertain what else to do.
The final breach came when the phone rang and Mara answered it. She removed her mask again, even though she knew she was not supposed to. It was only a supplier calling about a routine matter, but Mara heard an opportunity to negotiate a better deal. Confident in her own abilities, she handled it herself, believing Philippe would appreciate her initiative even while she knew she was breaking his explicit rule to keep mask and gag on.
When Philippe returned later that day, the first sign that something was wrong came the moment he stepped into his office. The files, now reorganized according to Mara’s system, were not where he expected them to be. He opened drawers and found nothing where it belonged, frustration building with each misplaced document. It did not take long for him to understand who was responsible.
His anger simmered as he moved through the house, noticing the changes in staff routine and the uneasy looks they gave him as he passed. By the time he reached the study, his patience had worn thin.
“Mara, come here,” he called, his voice colder than she had ever heard it.
Mara, who had been in her room arranging papers of her own, felt a chill run down her spine at the tone. She hurried to the study, where Philippe stood by his desk, his expression hard and unforgiving.
Yes, Sir? she signed calmly, though her heart was racing.
Philippe wasted no time.
“What have you done?”
Mara blinked, startled by the directness of it. Her hands moved.
I thought helping. Files disordered, so I…
“Without asking me?” Philippe interrupted, his eyes narrowing. “You went through my office, rearranged my things, and gave orders to my staff, all without consulting me.”
Mara felt shame rising into her face. Her hands moved again.
Only trying make things smoother. I thought…
“That is the problem, Mara. You did not stop at thinking. You did.” His voice cut cleanly through her explanation. “I have told you repeatedly that you are not to make decisions on behalf of this household or my business without my express permission. You may make suggestions. I decide.”
Mara tried once more.
But I was only…
Philippe raised a hand and stopped her.
“Enough. Your actions today have shown me that the last correction was not effective. You still believe you can act as you please, regardless of the rules I have set.”
Mara’s heart sank. She knew she had overstepped, but the realization that she had pushed Philippe too far struck harder than she expected. She had been so focused on fixing what looked inefficient that she had ignored the boundaries he had set. The worst part was that she had done it knowingly. She had wanted to prove that she could still be useful, still take charge. Standing before him now, she saw how wrong she had been.
Philippe took a breath, his anger still visible in the tightness of his jaw.
“You have shown me that you are not ready to accept your role fully, Mara. The corrections I have given you so far have not worked. It is clear that something more permanent is needed.”
Mara’s eyes widened.
“Permanent?”
“Yes,” Philippe said. “You need a reminder that will help you understand the importance of the rules, proper behavior, and your role in this household. At all times. Every second.”
Regret, failure, and fear moved through her together. She had tried so hard to balance who she used to be with the new expectations placed on her, and it seemed she had only made things worse. She searched his face for some sign of leniency and found none.
“Please,” she began, then stopped, because she did not know how to finish. What could she say that would change his mind?
Philippe shook his head, his expression softening only slightly.
“Mara, this is not meant as punishment. You need help to find your place, the place this world wants to see you in. Your independence, while admirable, does not fit with the role you have chosen. I will help you learn, but you must understand that learning will come with discomfort.”
Mara nodded, throat tight. She had no choice but to accept what was coming. She had chosen this path when she asked to become Philippe’s ward, fully aware of the responsibilities and rules it carried. She had repeated those rules back to him, understanding that his role as guardian meant keeping her from acting in ways that would be socially unacceptable. Now she saw that Philippe was simply fulfilling that duty.
The thought of something more permanent terrified her, but there was no going back. She had to trust Philippe, even if that trust meant surrendering more of herself than she had imagined.
I understand, she signed slowly.
Later that same day, Philippe sat comfortably on the couch, watching the latest product presentation from Cupertino on the living room TV. Mara knelt at his feet, posture perfect, eyes fixed on the screen. The event seemed to be wrapping up when the presenter paused and announced, “One more thing.” Philippe leaned forward slightly, intent.
“Today, we are proud to introduce our venture into the domestic chastity and discipline market: the iGuardian,” the presenter said.
An image of sleek, high-tech metal panties appeared on the screen under the slogan Make her think different. Mara felt a chill run down her spine.
The original iGuardian device was presented as a marvel of restraint technology: a steel or titanium panty fitted with electrodes and attachments for long-term wear. It had a catheter, an anal cleanser, and flexible vaginal stimulators, all controllable by Bluetooth. Guardians could monitor bodily functions, set geofences, schedule cleansing cycles, dispense rewards or discipline, log GPS data, authorize pre-approved purchases and transport passes, and even guide a ward with steering impulses.
Then the presenter revealed the iGuardian Pro Secure.
A full-body corset with built-in components: an integrated collar and neck corset, overbust covers, and chastity panties. Designed for long-term wear, it offered more sensors, better electrodes, longer battery life. The Guardian Pro App promised extensive oversight, detailed metrics, and an extraordinary degree of control.
Mara’s breath caught as the meaning settled over her. The clean design. The control. The discipline. It was obvious. This was her future. Philippe had been patient, but she had pushed too far, and the iGuardian Pro Secure would be her consequence.
She could feel his gaze on her. She had overplayed her hand, and now she faced the ultimate correction. The idea of being so completely controlled, of having every movement and function monitored, filled her with dread and a reluctant sense of acceptance.
Philippe rested a hand on her shoulder.
“Mara,” he said softly, “this is what happens when you overstep your bounds.”
Mara nodded slowly.
Yes, Sir.
His grip tightened just a little.
“You need this, Mara. For your own good.”
She closed her eyes for a moment, trying to steady herself.
I understand, Sir.
The presentation went on, but Mara hardly saw it anymore. The iGuardian Pro Secure would ensure her obedience, her submission, and her place at Philippe’s feet, exactly where the new world said she belonged.
The store was buzzing with activity, the last touches of construction barely finished in time for the opening. The newly added floor held a state-of-the-art fitting center for iGuardian devices. Everything about it was designed for precision. Each ward would be 3D scanned in a private cabin so the fit could be exact.
A shop assistant called Audrey approached them, her uniform immaculate, her face concealed by a company-issued mask. She curtsied to Philippe, and he introduced himself without acknowledging Mara. He confirmed the appointment for “a fitting of an iGuardian Pro Secure for my ward,” while Mara stood motionless at attention.
Audrey explained the fitting process to Philippe and then politely requested that he undress his ward in the changing cabin and guide her into the scanning booth. Philippe did exactly as she asked, calm and dispassionate. Mara complied without hesitation, anxious but silent. She stood still while Philippe undressed her and felt the cold air against her skin as she stepped completely bare into the scanner.
The booth offered only a brief illusion of privacy. The machine hummed softly while laser grids moved over her skin, capturing every contour of her body with exact precision. A synthesized female voice instructed her into pose after pose, each one exposing her body to the scanner’s eye. When it was done, the booth opened, and Philippe dressed her in the hooded robe provided by the store.
Audrey explained the options available in the iGuardian line.
“Good afternoon, Sir,” she signed. “The iGuardian offers a range of customization options to suit your needs. Given your interest in control and discipline, I will outline the advanced features.”
She explained that the Pro Secure was designed for long-term wear and incorporated advanced monitoring, hygiene management, and both reward and correction systems. The control app, she added, allowed complete behavioral oversight through customizable programs and precise stimulation.
For the first time since entering the store, Philippe turned his attention to Mara.
“You may choose the color.”
It was the only decision she would be permitted to make.
Mara looked over the options Audrey displayed: feminine Rose Gold, timeless Pearl White, rich Midnight Blue, vibrant Emerald Green. After a moment she signed her choice.
With your approval, Rose Gold, please, Sir.
Philippe nodded. Audrey recorded it.
“An excellent choice,” she signed. “We will prepare the device for fitting.”
There was a short wait. Audrey served Philippe coffee while Mara knelt at his feet. Eventually Audrey returned and led them to the fitting room, where a Rose Gold iGuardian Pro Secure awaited them.
She presented the device to Philippe, each piece gleaming in its pristine finish.
“Undress,” Philippe told Mara. “Audrey will help you put it on.”
Mara complied, moving mechanically as she took off the robe. Audrey guided her through the fitting. Mara had to lie down, legs spread and fully exposed. Anxiety, vulnerability, and anticipation moved through her together.
Audrey began with the panty section and asked whether Mara preferred to be restrained for this part of the fitting. Mara declined. She wanted to face it unbound.
The catheter came first.
“Try to relax,” Audrey signed.
A light sting told Mara the insert had found its place. Then a small balloon expanded, filling her bladder enough to leave her with the constant feeling that she needed to urinate.
The vaginal insert followed, prewarmed and lubricated, thick and short, its head studded with sensors and electrodes. It spread her lips, but its stubby shape promised nothing satisfying.
Finally Audrey applied more lubricant and inserted the anal cleanser. It was wider than Mara had expected, and she had to work to relax enough to let it in. It slid into place with hard invasive pressure that made her wince. Once the widest part passed her sphincter, her own muscles drew it deeper.
The catheter and anal inserts were secured beneath a titanium shield that locked over them and clicked into the hip brace, forming a strict high-cut metal panty. An additional removable vaginal shield was placed on top, securing the vaginal insert.
Audrey explained to Philippe that he could remove the vaginal shield in two stages, using either the app or a key. Stage one would allow access while maintaining maximum shielding, denying the ward relief. Stage two would remove the clitoral cover as well, allowing fuller stimulation and eventual release at the guardian’s discretion.
When the shield was back in place, Audrey turned to Mara.
“Is the fit good?” she signed, her manner gentle but professional. “It is normal to feel full, but there must be no chafing, and it should not be painful.”
Mara nodded, already trying to adjust to the foreign sensations.
Audrey moved on to the corset section, positioning it around Mara’s torso, clicking it into place, and securing it against the hip brace of the chastity panty. As the self-tightening mechanism activated, the titanium mesh constricted slowly, molding itself to her shape until it looked like a smooth solid metal corset. The pressure was immediate, forcing her to stand taller, straighter.
Then Audrey fitted the breast covers, locking Mara’s chest into unyielding metal domes.
“These provide coverage and lift,” she signed to Philippe. “This is the classic shape, but there are other options, including a 1950s cone profile and a reduction variant. The covers are easily interchangeable, so different dress silhouettes can be achieved without much effort.”
Philippe only nodded.
“These are fine for now. Please continue.”
Next came the optional shoulder braces and the discipline neck corset. Together they connected to the top of the corset front and back, covering her upper body and giving the whole device the look of a high-cut metallic racerback suit. Philippe had insisted on these additions, and Mara could feel their enforcement of a regal posture before the fitting was even complete. Audrey straightened each attachment, then adjusted the integrated neck corset, its memory-metal structure pulling close around Mara’s throat.
“The inconvenience is normal, as this is a restriction by design,” Audrey signed. “Your body will internalize the limited range of movement and the permanent posture. In a few months, it will feel normal.”
Mara doubted it. Nothing about this felt normal. Then again, perhaps that was exactly the point.
She tried to nod and could not, then signed that she understood. Her mind struggled to grasp the permanence of her new state.
Audrey continued explaining the device during short pauses.
“This device is safe for long-term use,” she signed. “It is self-cleaning, monitors your health data, and supports a skincare routine. It may feel restrictive, especially in the Pro Secure variant, but it should not be painful outside discipline mode.”
