“Next, we have an exclusive vacation package to a private island in the Maldives, donated by Leonardo DiCaprio,” Charles announced, shifting smoothly to the next lot.
Zendaya, moving carefully on rigid knees, presented it with a flourish while images of beaches and luxury villas glowed behind her.
“Bidding starts at twenty thousand euros.”
As the bids climbed again, Philippe leaned slightly toward Mara.
“The enthusiasm tonight is extraordinary. The money raised will do a great deal of good.”
Mara nodded, her eyes shining.
Yes, Sir. Wonderful see such generosity. This will make significant impact.
The auction continued, one item after another fetching impressive sums. Mara and Philippe watched with deep satisfaction, both of them knowing how much work had gone into making the evening succeed.

title: Chapter 42: Two years earlier: Breaking Point
content:
Two years earlier: Breaking Point# Mara knelt on her cushion on the polished marble floor of Philippe’s study, her back perfectly straight, her hips held upright, and her shoulders drawn back in the exact posture the iGuardian demanded. She had grown accustomed to the way the Yoyah Sheengzoh underskirt constrained her legs, but it was sitting that had become difficult enough that she now avoided it whenever she could. Kneeling, she had learned, was much easier. It avoided the painful pressure of the crotch belt that shifted the whole iGuardian upward whenever she sat too far back in a chair, and it also presented a more submissive posture that Philippe seemed to appreciate.
Philippe was in the middle of a conversation with a visiting diplomat, his voice steady and authoritative as he discussed trade agreements. Mara remained silent, hands folded neatly in her lap, eyes lowered. She was the picture of calm composure, even though her muscles ached from the strain of holding herself in that precise position for so long.
When the diplomat made a sharp remark, questioning one of Philippe’s decisions, Mara’s instinct was to answer, to defend Philippe, to correct the visitor’s tone. But she caught herself, knowing that an outburst would only earn her a painful correction from the iGuardian. Instead she focused on her breathing, keeping it steady, and when Philippe acknowledged her with a glance, she answered with a polite affirmative sign and nothing more.
When the meeting ended, Philippe dismissed the diplomat and turned to Mara.
“You may stand now,” he said, offering her a hand.
Mara rose slowly, careful to keep her posture perfect as she did. She moved with a dancer’s grace, each step measured, her weight precisely controlled. Over the past few weeks she had learned how to rise without disturbing the balance the iGuardian enforced.
Philippe studied her for a moment, then gestured toward a pair of boots on a nearby stool.
“Today we are going to try something different,” he said.
Mara looked down at them.
Ballet boots, with an impossibly high arch that forced the wearer onto her toes.
A flicker of apprehension ran through her, but she pushed it down at once. She had learned not to question Philippe’s decisions. Instead she waited silently as he retrieved the boots and motioned for her to sit.
Mara lowered herself carefully onto the edge of a nearby chair. Philippe knelt and changed her boots for the new ones. The moment she tried to stand, her balance shifted dramatically, her body forced into a position that felt all too familiar.
“Up on your toes now,” Philippe said, guiding her into place. “You will find this helps your posture.”
Mara stood, feeling the stretch pull through her calves as the boots forced her en pointe. The sensation was uncomfortable and strangely familiar, reminding her of her years as a ballet student. She adjusted her stance, concentrating on balance, and found that the boots did indeed make it easier to hold the posture Philippe expected. The arch forced her hips upright, while her chest was naturally pushed out as her body aligned itself with the iGuardian’s demands.
“Good,” Philippe said, stepping back to observe her. “You see? These boots will help you maintain the correct posture with less effort.”
Over the next few days, Mara grew used to the ballet boots. She found herself moving with even greater grace, the habits of ballet merging with the demands of the iGuardian to produce a new kind of fluidity. She knelt more often, preferring the ease of it to sitting, and her posture began to feel almost natural.
Then one day, as Mara stood before Philippe with perfect posture and her hands folded neatly in front of her, he looked her over with a pleased expression.
“I must say, Mara, I am impressed,” he said, calm and even. “Your behavior has improved significantly. You are a different woman now, thanks to the iGuardian. Who would have thought it could be so simple?”
Simple.
The word struck her like cold water.
Simple.
Did he truly think that was what he had done to her? The months of pressure. The shell. The feeding. The humiliation of being managed down to posture, appetite, sleep, and silence. Did he truly believe all of that had become simple because she had learned to hold still beautifully while it happened?
The anger rose too fast to contain. Her hands flew up before caution could catch them. The signing was vicious, stripped of elegance, full of the old Mara’s temper and vocabulary. She told him what he had reduced. What he had enclosed. How much of every day was spent enduring. How every graceful line he admired had been bought by force. The gestures turned coarse and ugly under the weight of it. She wanted him to see that whatever he thought he had achieved, he was not looking at peace. He was looking at strain made presentable.
Even as she signed, Mara knew she had made a terrible mistake.
The iGuardian detected her defiance almost at once and switched into discipline mode. Pain shot through her body, hard and searing, as the electrodes in her most sensitive areas came alive. The shocks were harsh, punishing her for the outburst. But despite the pain, Mara’s resolve did not collapse. She gritted her teeth, her body tensing, and forced herself through it the same way she had forced herself through pain all her life.
Philippe watched her closely, his expression changing as he observed her response. When the shocks finally stopped, Mara stood trembling, not from fear but from the sheer physical toll. Her anger still burned beneath the surface, now mixed with deep frustration. The pain had not taught her what Philippe had hoped it would.
Philippe saw it at once when the correction ended. She was shaking, but she was still looking at him with the same furious clarity. Held, not changed.
He did not say much. He only took out the control phone, glanced once at the screen, and made a different selection.
With a firm tap, he activated the program.
The iGuardian immediately changed what it was doing to her.
The sensation took Mara by surprise so completely that for a second she did not even understand it. Then her breath caught. Her legs weakened. The stimulation landed with a precision that left no room to dismiss it as anything but deliberate. It found her, held her, and kept holding her just short of anything she could complete.
Her body reacted before thought did. Her thighs tightened. Her breathing turned quick and shallow. One hand drifted downward on instinct and stopped halfway because the prohibition against touching herself was already too deeply learned to break cleanly. She did not know where to put her hands after that. They hovered, opened, closed, moved uselessly at the edges of her body while the device kept her in that bright impossible state.
Pain she could organize herself against. This was harder to oppose because it crowded her from the inside. The teasing pressure adapted each time she tried to settle around it. There was no clean peak, no clean failure, only mounting need and the humiliating fact that her body had become fully legible to whatever program Philippe had just chosen.
“Mara,” Philippe said quietly, watching her closely, “you will learn. You are already on your way.”
Mara did not answer. She was too overwhelmed by what the iGuardian had discovered how to do to her.
As the days passed, the iGuardian continued its conditioning. Mara learned quickly that defiance or carelessness led to the loss of the stimulation she had begun to crave. That absence alone was enough to drive her toward more compliant behavior. The desire to be a good girl and keep that constant tantalizing thread alive became a force in her daily life. If she still resisted, the device could always return to pain, but pain mattered less now than the risk of losing what her body had started wanting.
Her posture, once something she had to think about constantly, became automatic. Her voice and signing grew more polite, more careful, more deferential. She started looking for ways to please Philippe before she had fully admitted that was what she was doing.
Philippe noticed the change.
“You have come a long way, Mara,” he remarked one day, watching her kneel before him after a day of flawless behavior. “I hoped you would finally make progress, but you have exceeded my expectations.”
Mara’s hands moved smoothly and gracefully as she responded.
Thank you, Sir. With your guidance, I am trying be best I can be.
She knew she was being conditioned, trained into obedience, but there was no escape. Day by day the iGuardian stripped away her resistance, shaping her into the obedient, submissive woman society expected her to become.
Satisfied with her progress, Philippe decided to reward her. He leaned over, disabled edging mode, and set the device to deliver a full reward with release. Then he ordered her to come.
The sudden wave of pleasure left Mara breathless, her body trembling with the force of it. For a brief moment she hovered at the edge, then the release she had been denied for days crashed through her.
Philippe watched with clear satisfaction.
“Good girl, Mara,” he said warmly. “You have earned this.”
Still trying to catch her breath, Mara signed her gratitude.
Thank you, Sir.
The iGuardian remained in place, its control over her as unyielding as ever. Philippe had granted her a rare release, and it felt to Mara as though he had finally turned the relentless edging off.
At least, that was how it felt to her.
Unbeknownst to Mara, the mode continued to run in the background at a very low level, subtly shaping her behavior. The constant, barely noticeable stimulation remained, withdrawing whenever she drifted toward undesirable conduct. The conditioning continued beneath her conscious awareness, guiding her toward the submission she still needed to learn.

title: Chapter 43: Kidnapped!
content:
Kidnapped!# The Green Gala at the Ecoville Hotel was coming to an end. Guests, still excited from the evening, were making their way to their vehicles. Zendaya, enclosed in her metallic red fembot suit and covered with flowers and leaves, approached her hexacopter with Tom Holland’s help. By then the suit was almost completely locked, leaving her unable to move without assistance.
As Tom helped her into the aircraft, the sudden roar of engines tore through the night air. Two black motorbikes stopped nearby. Their riders, four figures in dark clothing wearing advanced breather masks, leapt off almost at once.
“Get away from her!” Tom shouted, stepping forward. One of the attackers shoved him to the ground.
“Get back, everybody!” another barked, waving a compact but very dangerous-looking weapon.
The crowd scattered in panic. The hexacopter’s engines spun up, blades accelerating. Zendaya, struggling in the suit, was strapped into her seat, her eyes wide with shock behind the fembot hood.
“Call the Grenadiers!” someone shouted.
Philippe, watching from a short distance away, pulled out his phone and called for help at once.
“We need immediate assistance at the Ecoville Hotel. There is a kidnapping in progress.”
As the hexacopter lifted off, the two remaining attackers revved their engines and tore away on their motorbikes, weaving between guests and racing down the grand driveway. Sirens answered almost immediately as the Grenadiers arrived in flashing light.
“Do not let them escape!” one officer shouted.
The chase spilled into Geneva’s narrow streets. The bikes darted through the web of side roads, cutting hard through corners. The Grenadiers followed close behind, using advanced tracking systems to keep pace.
One of the bikers, Eliza, looked back.
“They are gaining, Max! We need to split up!”
Max nodded.
“Take the left alley. I will pull them away.”
He veered right, drawing part of the pursuit after him. Eliza sped down a narrower street, her bike skidding as she forced it through the turn.
The Grenadiers split their teams. Some pursued Max, others followed Eliza. Max took one final corner and found Grenadiers in front of him while the others closed from behind. Cornered, he skidded to a stop, his bike crashing into a wall. He came up with the weapon still in hand as the officers closed around him.
“Drop it! You are surrounded!”
Max hesitated, then saw the truth of the situation and let the weapon fall. He raised his hands in surrender.
Eliza reached a dead end and tried to turn back, only to find the way blocked. She revved the bike once, measuring the distance, but the Grenadiers had already sealed her in.
“Stand down. There is nowhere to go,” an officer said as he stepped forward.
Eliza recognized him at once. Captain Duval, a man she had once respected before the Change. She let out a breath, knowing the fight was done, swung off the bike, and raised her hands.
Inside the hexacopter, Zendaya struggled in vain while a female captor held her down. The male captor at the controls flew low and unsteadily. Zendaya’s muffled attempts to speak went unheard. The female captor tightened her grip.
“Stay still. It will be easier for you.”
The hexacopter skimmed low over the dark waters of the lake before following the Rhône. It flew almost at treetop level, cutting through narrow valleys. The absence of pursuit confused the kidnappers, but they had no time to dwell on it. Eventually they veered into a side valley, followed the Lonza upstream, and headed toward the Aletsch Glacier. Then the pilot took the aircraft sharply down toward a tiny newly built hut beside a narrow landing pad.
The landing was rough in the high Alpine wind. The pilot exhaled in relief.
“Get her out. Quickly.”
The female captor dragged Zendaya across the pad and into the hut, then strapped her to a chair.
“We will be safe here for now,” she said, her voice muffled behind the breather.
Outside, the male captor folded the hexacopter and concealed it from view. Up there they were alone. Only the distant sound of running water broke the silence.
Inside, Zendaya’s eyes searched desperately for any way out. The gagged fembot hood restricted her vision, and she was bound thoroughly enough that movement was almost impossible. Her female captor kept glancing at the door.
“We have to move fast,” the man said as he came in and shut it behind him. “The Freeborn Alliance will send someone soon.”
He stepped toward Zendaya and removed the robotic headpiece with specialized tools. Zendaya gasped as the air hit her face.
“Help me, please,” she cried, tears already running down her cheeks. “It hurts.”
The man frowned in confusion.
“What hurts?”
“My belt,” she whimpered. “I am outside the geofence. It keeps shocking me.”
A stream of curses burst from him.
“Damn it. No wonder they did not follow us,” he muttered. “She is in an active chastity device. They all carry tracking beacons.”
He snapped his head toward his companion.
“Quick. Help me get it off her. We need to kill the beacon.”
They fumbled with the suit while Zendaya sobbed and twitched from the belt’s repeated shocks.
Then flashbangs detonated.
The hut exploded with white light and concussive sound. The kidnappers stumbled back, blinded and deafened, hands flying to their faces. The door burst inward, and a team from the Commandement des Forces Spéciales stormed the room in goggles and tactical gear, firing stun rounds as they moved.
“Clear!” one of them shouted once the room was under control.
Outside, helicopter blades thundered overhead. An Alpine rescue physician abseiled down, followed by more heavily armed special forces. The kidnappers were bound, dragged out of the hut, and hauled into the helicopter.
The emergency doctor moved straight to Zendaya. Using specialized equipment, he cut through the suit and then through the belt, finally freeing her. Zendaya cried out as the device came away.
“You are going to be all right,” the doctor said gently, administering a mild sedative and wrapping her in a warm blanket.
She was secured onto a rescue stretcher, lifted out of the hut, and winched into the helicopter.
As the aircraft climbed and turned back toward Geneva, Zendaya’s eyes fluttered shut. Exhaustion and the sedative pulled her under. The ordeal was over. She was safe.

title: Chapter 44: After the Gala
content:
After the Gala# Mara’s day ended in the early morning hours, her body exhausted by the night’s events and the restrictive clothing she had worn. Every step had been a struggle, every smile something carefully balanced against the demands of the dress. The evening had begun with a crisis when Zendaya arrived bare-faced, breaking one of the most visible social rules. Mara had helped manage that, only to watch relief vanish when Zendaya was kidnapped by unknown terrorists. Now, as she prepared for bed, uncertainty about Zendaya’s fate left her deeply unsettled.
Philippe guided her to their suite, steadying her as she took unsteady steps. The stiff ballet boots gave her additional support, and she was grateful for it. The events of the night still weighed heavily on both of them.
When they entered the suite, they found Liliane asleep in a chair, still in uniform. Philippe woke her gently, and together they began removing Mara’s outfit. The headdress came off first, bringing welcome relief from its weight.
Philippe’s phone buzzed with a message. His face softened as he read it.
“Mara,” he said quietly, “Zendaya has been rescued. All four kidnappers have been caught.”
The tension went out of Mara’s body.
Thank God, she signed. Know who they were, or what they wanted?
Philippe shook his head.
“Not yet. They were well-equipped but badly trained. It is still unclear who they were or what they wanted.”
Mara hand-danced her disappointment and unease.
Unsettling think such well-funded group is out there.
“I know,” Philippe said, squeezing her hand. “But for now Zendaya is safe, and the immediate danger is over. We will learn more in time.”
She tried to take comfort from that.
Hope so. This night much more than expected.
Philippe gave her a reassuring smile.
“We will handle it, Mara. Together.”
They continued the careful business of undressing her, removing the stiff layers that had encased her all evening. With each piece that came away, Mara felt both relief and a growing vulnerability. Philippe supported her while Liliane worked each part of the dress free.
Once the outer costume was gone, Philippe and Liliane finished undressing her until only the iGuardian remained. Then Philippe dismissed Liliane with the dismantled dress and wished her good night.
Without the elaborate outfit, the iGuardian left Mara feeling exposed. Philippe slipped a pair of high heels onto her feet. After years in ballet heels, flat shoes were out of the question. The height felt almost comfortable by comparison.
He led her into the bathroom for a quick wash. The iGuardian handled most of the process, but Philippe washed the exposed skin with his own hands, gentle and careful. The warmth of the water and the steadiness of his touch eased some of the tension from her body. He removed her mask so she could brush her teeth, then guided her to the bed.
As always, he had her kneel beside it so he could do her hair. He undid the bun, loosened the braids, and gave it only the care it truly needed, sensing how exhausted she was. His fingers moved through it with practiced skill, lulling Mara toward sleep. She was almost gone by the time he relaxed the collar, braces, and corset of the iGuardian, lifted her into bed, and cuffed her hands in front of her, making sure she was secure without being uncomfortable.
Mara barely noticed when Philippe settled against her from behind, his warm body a comfort against the hard titanium line of the iGuardian. His presence kept the nightmares of the kidnapping at bay. Instead she dreamed only of the evening’s successes, safe in the knowledge that Philippe would protect her.
She woke again before dawn, the room still dark. The only sound was Philippe’s quiet breathing behind her. She felt the firm embrace of the iGuardian, the elevation of her feet in heels, and the restriction of the cuffs. Even so, she felt vulnerable. Her legs were bare, her arms were ungloved, her mouth was empty, and her face was uncovered. That exposure unsettled her.
As she stirred, Philippe woke, sensing the discomfort in her body. He shifted closer in silent comfort. Mara took a breath and spoke softly.
“Sir, may I please have my mask?”
Her voice, almost unused over the last three years, came out hoarse. She hated speaking, preferring the elegance and precision of hand-dancing, but with her hands cuffed she had no other way to communicate.
“I feel insecure without it.”
Philippe understood immediately.
“Of course, Mara,” he said gently.
He reached to the nightstand, picked up her Jurenmuse, and turned back to her. He placed the gag into her mouth and locked the mask to her collar. The snug fit and enclosing pressure around her face made her feel safer at once.
“Thank you, Sir,” Mara tried to say, but only a pleased muffled sound escaped.
Philippe smiled and caressed her shoulder.
“You are welcome, Mara. Better now?”
Mara cuddled back against him as much as the stiff iGuardian allowed, deeply relieved. The warmth of his body and the security of the mask let her relax again.
She drifted back into sleep, her mind at ease. The protective iGuardian and Philippe’s presence let her surrender to the darkness feeling safe, loved, and cared for.
The next morning, Philippe guided her through the usual cleaning and dressing routine with patient care. He helped her into stockings and gloves, checking that every seam lay straight. After fastening a high-collared blouse and hobble skirt around her, he dressed her in another Victorian bustle gown.
“Ready, Mara?” Philippe asked softly, checking the fit one last time.
Yes, Sir, she signed.
Philippe activated her iGuardian’s guidance, and it sent her down to the breakfast room. She stood waiting at the entrance in line with other women waiting for their guardians. When Philippe arrived, he led her to his table and locked her into her chair.
A maid in hotel livery, her name plate reading Iris, responded to Philippe’s signal. She attached a feed bag to the port on Mara’s mask and began serving Philippe his breakfast. Mara felt the feed gag expand in her mouth, the nutrient liquid spurting down her throat in familiar measured pulses. Her swallowing was automatic by now, drilled into her by years of repetition.
A few minutes later, Sonia and Henry entered. Henry, elegant in a stylish suit, waved to Philippe, who motioned them over.
“Good morning, Philippe,” Henry said. “Good morning, Mara.”
“Good morning, Henry. Sonia,” Philippe replied.
Henry locked Sonia into the chair opposite Mara so the two women could see each other. Sonia’s dress was equally elaborate, though closer-fitting: a blouse buttoned in the back and a floor-length mermaid skirt. For breakfast she wore a niqab that allowed her to eat rather than a mask. As soon as she was secured, her eyes met Mara’s, and they began signing at once.
Heard about Zendaya? Sonia signed, concern clear in her face.
Mara nodded.
Yes. Philippe told me this morning. She was rescued, and all four kidnappers were caught.
Henry leaned toward Philippe.
“What do we know about them?”
Philippe shook his head.
“Very little so far. They were well-equipped but badly trained. We do not know their motives yet. It is unsettling.”
Sonia signed quickly, concern tightening her eyes.
Poor Zendaya. Know how she is?
“Safe, and apparently unharmed,” Philippe assured her. “She is being cared for and should return soon.”
Relief passed between the two women at once.
Thank goodness she is safe. Last night terrifying, Mara signed.
Henry nodded.
“We will need to stay vigilant. If one group was willing to go that far, there may be others.”
Philippe agreed.
“Absolutely. We must protect everyone and be prepared for future threats.”
Sonia, sensing how heavy the mood had become, shifted the conversation with a trace of a smile in her signing.
See Zendaya’s outfit last night? Despite everything, transformation fascinating. From scandalously bare-faced woman to increasingly robot-like figure, all while still incorporating nature. Quite spectacle.
Mara nodded.
Yes, intriguing. Outfit became increasingly strict and mechanical. Amazing how fashion can express those contrasts. Also reminded me how important flexibility and muscle strength remain when wearing something as restrictive as robot suit, or my iGuardian.
Sonia’s eyes lit up.
Exactly. Strictness of our dress demands different fitness. Reminded me of Julien Moreau’s Anna. Before Change she ran. Now she stays fit with pony training. Rigorous, but effective.
Mara’s interest sharpened.
Pony training? Heard of it, but never saw practice. How work for her?
Sonia signed with real enthusiasm.
Fascinating. Anna wears special suit that restricts her and has guide bit like pony. She is put before sulky, and Julien guides her through endurance course. Combination of physical training and discipline.
Mara nodded thoughtfully.
Sounds challenging and intriguing. Would like learn more. Maybe arrange visit?
Sonia’s hands moved eagerly.
Sure Anna happy show you. She adapted well and enjoys training now.
The conversation flowed easily, their hands saying what voices did not. Henry and Philippe watched them with quiet approval.
Philippe turned to Henry.
“It is good to see them connecting. They have much to share. Pony training sounds interesting. Mara could use more strength work. She focuses so much on mobility at the moment.”
Henry nodded warmly.
“It is demanding. It began as a discipline program for problematic women, meant to build obedience and submission and keep them physically exhausted. But many well-adjusted women do it now for fitness.”
Philippe and Henry agreed that they would look into the practice for their wards soon.

title: Chapter 45: A Day at the Races
content:
A Day at the Races# The opportunity came the following weekend when Philippe and Henry took their wards to the pony track. As they arrived, the place buzzed with excitement and order. The clinking of metal and leather being adjusted added to the strict atmosphere.
Anna was already on the track, dressed in her full pony outfit. Her catsuit was a striking shade of deep green, highlighting her toned body. The suit was seamless, with built-in gloves and feet, and her hair was pulled through a hole in her open-faced hood, cascading down her back. The suit left her derrière exposed, with only her chastity belt offering any modesty—a tempting target for the crop.
Over the catsuit, she wore a thick leather corset, dyed dark brown, cinching her waist tightly. It had attachment points at her hips for the sulky.
Her head was encased in an elaborate bridle, with cheekpieces, a noseband, and a throatlatch holding a bit in her mouth. The bit acted as a gag, preventing any speech. Originating from a discipline and obedience training program, it was made from rubber, but contained steel needles on the inside. It guided her, but if she resisted, the needles pressed into her mouth.
A wide, thick leather collar around her neck prevented any head movement, forcing Anna to follow the reins with her whole body. Blinkers attached to the cheekpieces restricted her vision, making her rely entirely on Julien’s guidance. An impressive plume matching her catsuit crowned her headstall.
Anna’s hands were locked to the sides of her corset with rigid leather arm sheaths, rendering them useless. Her feet were encased in knee-high pony boots, forcing her into an elevated foot position. The boots had heavy irons underneath.
Julien, her guardian and driver, adjusted the final straps and reins with care. He tested their tension with a gentle tug, ensuring they were responsive without immediately causing pain.
“Ready, Anna?” Julien asked, knowing she couldn’t respond verbally.
Anna’s gaze, narrowed by the blinkers, remained fixed ahead as she stood perfectly still, waiting for his command. Julien attached the sulky to her corset, securing it firmly and testing the connection. Satisfied, he took his place in the sulky, reins in hand.
“Walk on,” Julien commanded, touching Anna’s rear with the crop and letting the rein drop a bit.
Anna responded instantly, her body moving forward at the signal. She pulled the sulky towards the oval racetrack, her steps slow and cautious due to the weight of the cart and her restrictive outfit. Julien used the crop again, gently tapping her exposed rear, urging her to pick up the pace.
“Good girl, Anna. Keep going!” Julien encouraged.
Anna increased her pace, her legs working harder despite the strain of the pony boots and the weight of the irons. The blinkers limited her view, but she moved confidently, trusting Julien’s guidance. As they reached the track, Julien used the crop more frequently, tapping her rear to signal a faster pace.
“Go, go, go! Trot!” he ordered, his voice calm but firm.
Anna shifted to a trot. The irons under her boots clinked with each step, and her muscles strained under the effort. Julien maintained a gentle but firm grip on the reins, guiding her with precision. Any hint of disobedience was met with a sharper pull on the reins, a painful reminder to stay focused and compliant. Occasionally, he used the crop more sternly, delivering stinging corrections to her exposed rear.
Philippe and Henry watched with keen interest, noting Julien’s balanced approach of care and discipline with Anna. Philippe turned to Henry, clearly approving. “She’s well-trained. Julien has done an excellent job with her,” Philippe remarked.
Henry nodded, his eyes on Anna. “Indeed. She’s adapted well to the training. The discipline and control are impressive.”
Mara and Sonia, standing beside their guardians, observed silently. Mara was especially intrigued by the intensity of the training and the level of control Julien maintained. Sonia signed to Mara, her eyes wide with fascination.
That, someday, this one would like to try. Looks intense. Rewarding too.
Mara nodded, clearly interested, then signed back. Perhaps that can be arranged. It would be a good challenge.
As Julien guided Anna around the track, her pace steadily increased. The physical and mental demands of the training were clear in her every movement. Despite the harshness of the exercise, there was a sense of purpose in her stride.
“Let’s pick up the pace. Go, go, go,” Julien commanded, giving Anna free rein.
Anna responded, her steps becoming more rhythmic and powerful. Julien’s guidance remained steady, his commands clear. The sulky moved smoothly behind her, showing off her strength and training.
After completing a fast-paced lap, Julien pulled the reins in a bit, slowing Anna to a controlled trot. The session continued, with Julien alternating between encouraging touches and sharper corrections, keeping a balance between discipline and support. After half an hour, it was clear Anna had reached her limits.
Philippe and Henry exchanged glances, impressed by the display of control and endurance. They knew this kind of training required not just physical strength but also mental toughness—qualities they valued highly in their wards.
As the session ended, Julien slowed Anna to a walk, allowing her to cool down. He dismounted and began unbuckling the straps, removing the reins. Anna stood still, her body trembling with exhaustion but her posture disciplined.
“Good work, Anna,” Julien said gently. “You did well today. Good girl!” Anna’s eyes, visible through the blinkers, showed her relief. She closed them as the praise triggered her conditioned response. The training had been tough, but she had endured and performed admirably.
Philippe turned to Mara, his voice filled with anticipation. “Are you interested in trying this, Mara? I have the necessary attachments for your iGuardian. It will be challenging, but I believe you can do it.”
Mara nodded, her eyes reflecting her determination, and signed. Yes, Sir. This one is ready.
Sonia looked startled and signed her confusion. Why need that…? Ah. You are in a Pro Secure. This one did not realize. That is much more discipline than expected.
Philippe turned to her. “Yes, she is. But I have the pony training attachments available for it. We’ll see.”
Henry then turned to Sonia. “And you, would you like to try if we can find a fitting bridle in the stable?”
Sonia signed her answer. Gladly, Sir, but if it pleases you, not in someone else’s suit.
Henry interrupted, “I know. As it happens…” He reached into the leather bag he carried and pulled out a pony training catsuit he had brought for her. Sonia’s eyes widened as she realized she had been set up.
While Julien helped Anna clean up and get dressed again, Henry guided Sonia to the changing area. There, he dressed her in a setup similar to what Anna had worn earlier. Sonia’s mind raced as she realized just how intense this was going to be.
Mara’s setup was simpler. The iGuardian already provided all the restraint and control necessary. Philippe added a bright pink latex catsuit over the device, ensuring it clung tightly to her form, highlighting her curves.
He then attached sulky connectors to the slots at her hips, clicking them securely into place. Next, Philippe laced her feet into knee-high pony boots, their elevated heels bringing her feet into a position she was used to.
Mara remained still, her hands folded neatly behind her back, as Philippe removed her regular mask and replaced it with a horse mask, complete with a pink plume. The mask was made of thick leather, with a built-in gag that filled her mouth. It clicked into the collar of her neck corset, fixing it in place. Finally, Philippe cuffed her hands behind her back. The restraints were simple but effective, leaving Mara with no way to resist or adjust herself.
Philippe guided her outside slowly, towards the sulkies. Sonia was already there, harnessed and waiting. Mara’s heart pounded in her chest, but she was ready for what was to come.
Philippe carefully attached the sulky to the fasteners on Mara’s iGuardian, making sure everything was secure. He then settled into the seat, holding a small controller connected via Bluetooth to her “virtual reins.” These “reins” sent impulses directly to Mara’s iGuardian, controlling the electrodes buried deep in her body and over her breasts. The impulses would guide her, signaling which direction to turn, when to speed up, and when to slow down.
“Ready, Mara?” Philippe asked, his voice calm but with an edge of anticipation.
Mara pawed her hooves, though her nerves were taut. She had no idea how intense this control would be, but she was determined to master it.
Philippe took a deep breath and signaled her to move forward. A sharp jolt surged through Mara’s body, the gag choking her gasp. The signal in her anus was far stronger than she had expected, almost painful. She instinctively twisted in the wrong direction, trying to ease the discomfort, but it only made the impulse worse.
Philippe was quickly easing off the control. He hadn’t anticipated just how sensitive the system was.
Mara bit down on her gag, stoically waiting for commands. Philippe made another attempt, this time with a gentler touch. The impulse came again, this time more bearable, though still uncomfortable. It guided her forward and to the right, but she hesitated, unsure of how much to turn. Philippe adjusted the reins, and the signal became sharper, almost punishing. Mara winced, feeling the pain deep inside and on her right breast, as the breast cover activated too.
Philippe, sensing Mara’s distress, nodded, focusing on making his movements smaller. He moved the controller more carefully, and this time, the impulse was softer. Mara felt it guiding her, not forcing her. She turned to the right, moving the sulky along with her, feeling more in tune with the signal. But then Philippe tried to make her stop, and the sudden sharp impulse to her clit made her stumble, the pain almost bringing her to her knees.
Philippe pulled back completely. He took a moment to recalibrate the controls in his mind, trying to find the balance.
They tried again. Philippe sent a softer signal, and Mara moved as directed, turning smoothly this time. When he wanted her to stop, he carefully applied just a bit more pressure on the controller, and the signals from the iGuardian pulsed in a way that was firm but not painful. Mara slowed, coming to a controlled stop.
A look of relief crossed Philippe’s face as he saw they were finally in sync. Mara’s body relaxed slightly, the pain subsiding as she adjusted to the guidance. They both had a better understanding now—Philippe of the delicacy required, and Mara of how to read the signals.
“Got it,” Philippe murmured, more to himself than to her. He sent another command, and this time, Mara responded perfectly, moving the sulky forward with a steady pace. They were finally working together.
With the controls mastered, Philippe guided Mara to the track where Sonia, now in her own sulky with Henry as her driver, was waiting. Both women stood side by side, harnessed and ready, their eyes focused ahead. Mara was smaller and lighter than Sonia, but she felt the challenge in the air. Her competitive spirit flared, and she was determined to win this race.
Julien stood at the starting line, holding up a flag. He looked over at the two sulkies, his eyes scanning both women and their drivers. The tension in the air was thick as everyone prepared for the race.
Mara bit down again on her gag, determined to win and to prove herself, mastering this new challenge despite the pain and the control. She glanced at Sonia, who seemed just as determined, and then back at the track ahead.
Julien raised the flag, ready to start the race.
The race began with a burst of energy. Henry drove Sonia with sharp taps of the crop on her exposed rear, urging her forward with every strike. Philippe, on the other hand, guided Mara using the impulses from her iGuardian, sending pulses deep into her body to push her ahead. Both women started side by side, but it didn’t take long for the differences in their physical abilities to show.
Sonia, in her sleek black catsuit, surged ahead, her powerful legs propelling her forward with ease. Mara, in her bright pink suit, struggled to keep up. She pushed herself hard, trying to match Sonia’s pace, but the race quickly became a battle of raw power, something Mara lacked compared to Sonia’s larger frame.
Philippe sensed Mara’s determination, saw how badly she wanted to win, and he pushed her harder with the signals, trying to draw out every ounce of energy she had. Mara responded, digging deep, her body straining with the effort. Her strength was in her flexibility and endurance, skills honed through years of ballet and yoga, but this race demanded something else—pure, brute strength. Despite her best efforts, Sonia continued to pull ahead, her powerful strides eating up the distance between them.
Mara felt the gap widen, felt the looming sense of failure creeping in. Her competitive spirit clashed with the reality of her limitations, and no matter how hard she tried, she couldn’t close the gap. Her legs burned, her lungs screamed for air, but it wasn’t enough. She watched helplessly as Sonia crossed the finish line well ahead of her.
By the time Mara stumbled across the line, she was exhausted and devastated. The victory had been so far out of reach, and now the weight of her failure settled on her heavily.
Philippe led her back to the changing rooms in silence. He could see the tears welling up in her eyes, the pain of her defeat written all over her face. Once inside, he gently began cleaning her, wiping away the sweat and grime, then helped her change back into her normal outfit and day-mask. The whole time, Mara fought back her tears, but when she was finally dressed, she couldn’t hold them back any longer. She broke down, crying quietly, the sting of failure cutting deep.
Mara signed with trembling hands, tears streaming behind her mask. I am sorry, Sir. This one failed you.
Philippe, kneeling and sitting her down on his knee in the stable, gently supporting her with one arm, watched her hands move with a sense of sorrow. He placed a hand gently around her narrow waist, his voice soft and reassuring. “Mara, you didn’t fail me. Please don’t think that.”
Mara hesitated, her fingers moving slowly, as if she was unsure whether to continue. It feels that way, Sir. This one could not keep up. Not strong enough. Not even close to what Sir expected.
Philippe shook his head, his tone firm but kind. “What I expected was for you to give your best, and you did that. Winning wasn’t the goal. You showed determination and spirit, and that’s what matters to me.”
Mara’s hands stilled for a moment, the weight of his words sinking in. But then, with a soft, almost hesitant gesture, she signed, This one wanted Sir proud. Did not want to disappoint Sir.
Philippe’s expression softened even more, and he took one of her gloved hands in his. “Mara, you didn’t disappoint me. Your dedication and willingness to push yourself are what make me proud. You have nothing to be ashamed of. Enough for now.”
Mara nodded, her fingers moving slowly in a final sign. Thank you, Sir, for your understanding.
Later, the three women sat together on the veranda of Philippe’s villa in Cologny, each secured to her chair. Mara, masked and silent, was fed nutrients from a feed bag. Sonia and Anna, dressed in niqabs, carefully lifted their veils to enjoy their coffee and small slices of tarte tatin, the rich aroma of caramelized apples mingling with the fresh air.
Sonia signed to Anna. Today’s training, how was it? Out there, you looked amazing. How keep that speed so long?
Anna paused, then signed back, her movements slow and deliberate. This was mild. Usually Julien pushes much harder. Lately, obedience and endurance. In the discipline and routine, comfort is there.
Mara, watching the exchange, couldn’t help but snort behind her mask at the mention of comfort. She shifted slightly, the iGuardian pressing against her in all the familiar places. But Anna’s hands moved again, explaining further, her expression thoughtful.
Yes, comfort. Strange perhaps, but discipline and routine give purpose. When pulling the sulky, everything else falls away. The noise in the head, the doubts, all gone. Only body and Julien’s guidance remain. This one knows her place and what is expected. Inside those boundaries there is peace. Hard to explain, but in those moments this one feels most herself.
Mara paused. She had not expected such a deep and serious answer. Thinking about her last two years in the iGuardian, she realized she understood more than she wanted to admit. The device had forced her into a similar kind of routine, where every movement was controlled, every action measured. There was no space for doubt or indecision; the device didn’t allow it. In a way, she had also found a strange peace within those boundaries, a place where the struggle to meet Philippe’s expectations became her sole focus. But unlike Anna, Mara wasn’t sure if she could ever call that peace comforting.
Sonia, always curious, tilted her head slightly as she signed to Mara. Never before has this one met a woman in an iGuardian Pro Secure. What is it like?
Mara paused, considering how to respond. The iGuardian was a part of her now, something she lived with every moment of every day. She wasn’t sure how to explain it, but she would try.
Her hands began to move slowly, with deliberate care. It is constant. Every part monitored. Controlled. The device adjusts posture, movement, even thought at times. It is there to guide, correct, keep this one focused and disciplined.
Sonia’s eyes widened slightly as she signed back. Painful?
Mara signed a clear no, her hands moving smoothly through the air. Not when this one behaves as she should. But if she strays, if she forgets her place, it can be harsh. The impulses are strong. They teach. They keep her in line.
Anna, watching the exchange, nodded slightly, her eyes showing understanding. She signed, Sounds difficult, but also calming. To know what is expected. To have guidance all the time.
Mara hesitated, then nodded, her fingers echoing her agreement. It is. There is peace in it. This one does not have to decide right or wrong. The iGuardian decides for her. In its way, freeing.
Sonia’s hands paused before she signed again, her movements slow and thoughtful. This one never imagined it that way. Always thought it must feel restrictive.
Mara’s hands moved quickly in response. Restrictive, yes. But comforting too. No room for doubt. No room for error. Everything decided for this one. That is easier.
Sonia’s curiosity finally got the better of her. She glanced at Mara, her hands moving with a mix of concern and curiosity. If this one may ask: why are you in an iGuardian Pro Secure? She thought it was for women who disturb social harmony.
Mara’s eyes flickered with a mix of emotions, but she quickly masked them. Her fingers moved with careful precision. Choices were made that brought this one here, Sonia. Philippe was right to use it. He has every right to expect the highest standards from his ward, and the iGuardian reinforces those standards.
Sonia wasn’t entirely satisfied with the answer. She pressed on, her hands carrying a hint of persistence. But the rewards? Surely it is more than discipline only?
Mara hesitated, then signed, A ward silently enjoys what her guardian offers. Her movements were controlled, almost too controlled, as if she were holding something back.
Sonia and Anna exchanged glances, a flicker of amusement passing between them. Their fingers moved quickly, sharing a private joke, their eyes glinting with slightly lewd humor.
Mara watched them for a moment, then signed with calm resolve. Whatever you have heard, probably it is true. Sometimes harsh, yes, but this one does not wish to be without it anymore. She paused, her hands slowing as the weight of the admission settled. This was not always so.
Sonia and Anna looked at her, sensing there was more she hadn’t said. Mara met their gaze, her fingers moving with almost ominous weight. The device also has an edging mode. If discipline mode does not bring a ward in line, that one will.
As the sun set, casting a golden light over the veranda, Philippe approached, signaling it was time to go.
Sonia and Anna began exchanging their veils for masks. Philippe unlocked Mara and helped her to her feet, guiding her. Henry and Julien released Sonia and Anna, preparing to leave.
Philippe, holding Mara by his side, nodded to Henry and Julien. “Thank you for coming. It was a pleasure.”
Henry smiled. “Likewise, Philippe. We look forward to the next time.”
With final curtsies, the group parted ways. Philippe led Mara inside, while Henry, Sonia, Julien, and Anna walked toward the tram stop.
As they waited, Sonia turned to Anna, her hands moving subtly. The iGuardian in edging mode must be hard to bear. This one wonders what Mara did to merit it.
Anna nodded and signed back. This one cannot imagine that strain. She would lose her mind.
Their conversation was cut short by Henry, who caught Sonia’s small signs nonetheless and reprimanded her. “Sonia, no gossiping. I won’t tolerate it. Whatever Mara did, she’s been corrected, and that’s the end of it. You know better.”
Sonia quickly signed, Yes, Sir. This one apologizes. She knew exactly what kind of correction Henry might have in mind if she gossiped about edging, and she definitely didn’t want that experience. She hated being denied.
The tram arrived, and they boarded, finding locking seats for the women at the back. After clicking Sonia into place, Henry rested his hand on her shoulder, a reminder of his authority. Julien guided Anna to a seat opposite Sonia and locked her in.
As the tram began its journey, Sonia and Anna exchanged a few more silent gestures. Despite the restrictions, they found comfort in each other’s company. The ride home was quiet, filled with unspoken thoughts and the hope of future gatherings. For now, they found solace in knowing they weren’t alone.

title: Chapter 46: Two years ago: Decommissioning an Airport
content:
Two years ago: Decommissioning an Airport# Philippe stood by the large window of the villa, overlooking the garden where Mara was instructing the gardener. He watched her hands dance in the air, giving instructions, yet sticking to form in a way that came naturally to her now. The iGuardian had finally put to correct use, shaping her to the expectations of her role, but Philippe couldn’t help but reflect on how wrong he had been at the start.
He had thought pain would be enough to break her defiance, to mold her into the woman society expected her to be. But Mara wasn’t like the others. Pain had only made her more determined, more resistant. It was only when he discovered how to harness her desire, for release, but also for reward and for approval, that she began to change. Seeing her now, fully absorbed in her tasks, he realized how flawed his initial approach had been. He had underestimated her, not just in her resistance but in her potential.
As Mara continued her work, efficiently managing the household staff, Philippe allowed himself a moment of self-critique. He had kept her close, confined to the villa, thinking it was the best way to ensure she adjusted. He now recognized that decision for what it was—his own insecurity. He had been afraid to let her out, to risk her slipping back into her old ways. But Mara wasn’t meant to be contained; she needed something challenging, something that would engage her mind and give her a sense of purpose.
Philippe’s thoughts drifted to the city’s projects, the initiatives he had heard discussed in his network. Most weren’t suited to Mara, but then one idea came to him—the decommissioning of Geneva International Airport. The plan was to shrink it down to a heliport and find a new use for the vast space left behind. The soil was poisoned from years of pollution, and the task of rehabilitating it was daunting. But it was the kind of challenge that Mara could sink her teeth into, something that would demand the full extent of her abilities while keeping her within the bounds of what was socially acceptable for a Changed woman.
Philippe approached Mara as she finished her instructions to the gardener. He waited until she turned to him and began.
“Mara, I’ve been thinking about a project that might interest you,” Philippe began. “The decommissioning of Geneva International Airport. They’re reducing it to a heliport, but the land is heavily polluted. It needs a new purpose.”
Mara listened attentively. After thinking for a moment, she signed carefully. That sounds like a significant challenge, Sir. If it pleases you, perhaps the area might become a series of connected parks and community gardens. Modern biotechnology could help draw pollutants from the soil. In time, the concrete wasteland could become green space: edible plots, small parks, places that serve the community.
Philippe watched her, nodding slightly. “And how would you propose to manage this?”
Mara signed again, in precise and respectful movements. Sir, if it suits your plans, the project could also serve as a place of learning and rehabilitation for women like this one who are struggling to adjust. Such women could work in the garden and find purpose within a structured environment. It would give them clear goals and expectations, something to focus on. Of course, it would require careful planning and oversight.
She paused, then added, This one could draft a proposal. If it meets with Sir’s approval, Sir could present it to the city council. Funding might be secured through national sustainability programs. If Sir considers it appropriate, the project could align environmental and social needs.
Philippe considered her words, then smiled approvingly. “That sounds promising, Mara. If we move forward, I’ll need you to draft those proposals. I will check them over and use my contacts to present them. You’ll need to navigate the city’s bureaucracy, find the right funding sources, and ensure the project aligns with societal expectations. Maybe I will use you to convince a few key people. Are you prepared to handle that?”
Mara nodded and signed her agreement. Yes, Sir. This one would be honored to take on the task. She believes the project could truly benefit the community.
Philippe placed a hand on her shoulder. “Good girl. Start on the proposals. This is your project, but I’ll support you where needed. Make it count.”
Mara signed her thanks and curtsied. Thank you, Sir. This one will begin at once.
With that, Philippe turned and left her to her thoughts, confident that Mara’s brilliant mind would bring this project to life, and in doing so, help her and others find their place in this new world.
A few days later, as Philippe entered his study, he was surprised to find Mara kneeling next to his desk. She was secured to a fempad, her body locked in place by the post behind her. The locking mechanism attached not only to her corset but also to her neck corset, with her elbows and wrists pressed tightly into self-locking manacles. She couldn’t move, couldn’t do anything without his intervention. He had no way of knowing how long she’d been there.
Ignoring her for a moment, Philippe turned his attention to the stack of folders on his desk. Each was meticulously prepared: proposals for councilmen, social media campaigns, suggestions for the school and reformatory boards, grant applications for the national sustainability board. And then there was a purple folder—documents inside that should not exist and that he knew could be used to sway even the most stubborn council members or board officials. Philippe knew Mara was talented, even ruthless, but seeing this level of preparation for the community garden project was astonishing.
He took his time reviewing everything, letting her stay in her self-imposed confinement. She had gone to extraordinary lengths, even in how she restrained herself, ensuring complete immobilization without anyone’s help.
Finally, after carefully reading through all the documents, he leaned back in his chair, thoroughly impressed. He turned to Mara and began unlocking her wrists and arms, allowing her to move and sign again. Then he squatted down in front of her, looking her in the eye.
“Now, what is all this?” he asked.
Mara’s hands moved gracefully as she signed, her tone polite and hopeful. Sir, everything needed for the community garden project has been prepared. These folders contain proposals, strategies, and plans. If Sir approves, all of it may be used to move the project forward. This one wished to make everything ready for review.
Philippe nodded, watching her closely. “And locking yourself like this?”
Mara’s hands hesitated for just a moment before continuing. Sir, this one wanted to make sure she could take no action without Sir’s permission, so that she would keep proper form. This was the only way she could think of to ensure it absolutely.
Philippe considered her response, his gaze softening slightly. She had gone above and beyond, not just in her work but in her commitment to following his guidance.
“You’ve done an exceptional job, Mara,” he said, his voice steady. “This is impressive. You’ve thought of everything.”
Mara signed her thanks, her movements full of quiet hope. Thank you, Sir. This one only wants to help make the project a success.
Philippe smiled, finally releasing her other restraints. “You’ve certainly done your part. Let’s move forward with this. You’ve earned it.”
Mara rose, then curtsied, signing. Thank you, Sir. This one is ready to follow Sir’s lead.
The following weeks were a whirlwind of activity for Philippe. He sent out proposals, scheduled appointments, and made official presentations while also meeting key figures informally over dinner. Mara, meanwhile, executed the social media grassroots campaigns she had meticulously planned, carefully timing each release for maximum impact. Together, their efforts created a perfect storm of political pressure on the city council, which coincided with the arrival of several grants—most of them approved—offering a straightforward solution. The council, finding themselves cornered by public demand and the sudden availability of funding, had little choice but to greenlight the community garden project.
At a dinner at Councillor Laurent’s home, Philippe and the Councillor were seated outside on the veranda, each with a glass of wine in hand. The evening air was crisp, and the low hum of conversation drifted from inside the house. After some light small talk, the Councillor swirled his wine and shifted the conversation to business.
“So, Philippe,” Laurent began, “with the community garden project about to be approved by the city council tomorrow, we’ll need someone to lead it. Do you have anyone in mind?”
Philippe paused for a moment, glancing back inside the house. Through the large glass doors, he saw Mara and Councillor Laurent’s wife, Claire, signing animatedly to each other. Claire was dressed in a daring gown that pushed the boundaries of Changed society’s modesty standards. The vivid, blocking color patterns of her dress caught the eye, and the fabric barely covered enough to be considered compliant. Her half-mask was more of a decorative piece than an actual covering, and the tiny hat perched on her head seemed to mock the idea of modesty altogether.
Mara, in contrast, was dressed in a way that emphasized her submission and discipline. Her burgundy gown was rich and elegant, the deep color highlighting the strictness of her attire. The gown’s bodice was tightly corseted, cinching her waist severely and pushing her posture into perfect alignment. Matching gloves covered her arms up to her elbows, and a bonnet, tightly tied under her chin, framed her masked face. The mask itself was full, hiding every feature except for her expressive eyes, which flicked up occasionally to meet Philippe’s gaze before returning to Claire.
Philippe turned back to Laurent. “Mara would be my recommendation. Before the Change, she was a corporate contract lawyer, highly skilled. If you consider it appropriate to have a woman lead the project, she would be more than capable.”
Laurent took a sip of his wine, considering Philippe’s words. “That would be legally impossible under the new laws,” he said, his tone thoughtful. “But… there is a workaround. Philippe Beaumont, represented through his ward Mara, could be a viable solution. Under the reformed guardianship laws, you would bear full liability for her actions, but she could effectively lead the project.”
Philippe hesitated, weighing the implications. The responsibility would be immense, not only for the project but also for the legal and financial consequences of any missteps. Yet he knew Mara’s capabilities, her drive, and her attention to detail. She had already done the lion’s share of the work to bring the project to this point.
After a moment, Philippe nodded. “I agree,” he said firmly. “Mara will represent me in leading the project. I’ll take full responsibility.”
Laurent smiled, satisfied with the decision. “Then it’s settled. I’ll make the arrangements, and we’ll announce it after the council meeting tomorrow.”
As the men raised their glasses in a silent toast, Philippe glanced back at Mara once more. The flickering candlelight caught the gleam of her mask, and for a brief moment, he saw the determination in her eyes. He knew she was ready for this challenge, and he was prepared to stand behind her, no matter the cost.
The following day, the Community Garden Project was formally established at the City Council meeting and Philippe Beaumont, represented by his ward Mara, was appointed to lead it.

title: Chapter 47: Plans involving Art and Fashion
Chapter 48: A Night at the Opera
content:
A Night at the Opera# Philippe had arranged for a limousine with a driver for the evening. He helped Mara down the stairs, and the driver adjusted the fempad in the back to accommodate her voluminous dress. Despite the cumbersome outfit, Mara knelt and locked into the seat’s holding arms with ease, the security cushions positioned carefully to avoid ruining her attire. Philippe sat opposite her, and they headed to the Grand Théâtre. The twenty-minute drive from Cologny passed quickly.
Upon arrival, Philippe unlocked Mara and helped her out of the car and into the grand theater. The foyer was grand, with chandeliers casting a warm glow over marble floors and intricate woodwork. A sweeping staircase with rich red carpeting invited guests to the upper levels.
The atmosphere at the opera was one of refined elegance, wrapped in formality and ritual. Women in elaborate, restrictive dresses moved gracefully through the foyer, their faces hidden behind veils or ornate masks. The majority of them wore face masks and had their hands free so they could hand-dance, while those in veils were often manacled, their hands bound behind or in front of them. They would have to use voice to articulate their needs. The soft murmur of male voices was the only real sound, aside from the occasional clink of jewelry, chains, or the rustle of fabric.
By the bar, men stood beside high-top marble tables with cast-iron feet. The tables had steel rings in the center, where many guardians had leashed their wards. It was a common sight—women standing still, tethered by their wrists or collars, waiting patiently while their guardians mingled or visited the washroom. A line of tether bars stretched along one wall, with women held in place, their feet locked into heel restraints and hands secured behind them to manacle bars, while their guardians were occupied.
Mara watched quietly as a small commotion caught her attention. A young woman, her face hidden behind a delicate veil, used her voice—shrill and loud. This was unusual—most women tried to avoid using voice entirely, and when they needed to speak, they certainly wouldn’t be loud or use any of the words or phrases that Mara had overheard. Her guardian, calm but firm, motioned for her to stop, but she didn’t. He finally led her to a quiet corner, where she stood facing the wall, clearly expected to calm down before she could address him appropriately.
As her gaze drifted further through the foyer, she saw a family approach. A father led his wife and two daughters in a typical chain-train. He held a leash attached to his wife’s collar, and she, in turn, held the leash of their eldest daughter, who led her younger sister by another leash. All three women were dressed fashionably: sparkling dresses and highly decorated masks, their tight dresses making it seem as if they glided effortlessly toward their booth.
Philippe scanned the crowd and soon spotted Henry with Sonia. Henry’s classic style never seemed to go out of fashion. He wore a formal evening jacket with satin lapels and a red fez, adding a touch of whimsy. The bright color was striking against the monochrome palette of his outfit.
Sonia’s harem dress was crafted from delicate white chiffon veils. Each layer was sheer by itself, but together they provided just enough coverage, with a teasing hint of what lay beneath. The bodice featured a sweetheart neckline adorned with silver embroidery. Instead of leaving the midriff bare like a traditional harem-girl outfit, a sleek, silvery corset cinched her waist, offering both modesty and a sculpted silhouette. The corset was seamlessly integrated into the design, its polished surface reflecting the light and creating a striking contrast with the soft chiffon veils cascading over her figure.
The skirt, made of additional chiffon veils, flowed gracefully, hinting at the shape of her legs without fully revealing them. High heels and ankle manacles restricted her steps to small, elegant movements. Long, flowing sleeves ended in steel cuffs that connected her wrists to her waist at the back. A heavy steel collar encircled her neck, attached to a chain held by Henry. Her head was crowned with a white and silver fez that matched Henry’s, serving as the anchor for the many layers of veils. Though the veils were thin, together they almost—but not quite—obscured her face.
“Good evening, Henry,” Philippe greeted warmly. “Sonia, you look stunning.”
Sonia responded with a deep curtsy.
“Good evening, Philippe. Mara, it’s wonderful to see you,” Henry replied, smiling with pride at Sonia’s appearance. Mara curtsied deeply.
Mara couldn’t help admiring Sonia’s dress. The contrast between the soft floating veils and the cold steel chains was captivating. She signed formally to Henry. Good evening, Sir. Then she turned to Sonia. Sonia, you look like a vision.
Sonia turned toward Mara. “Thank you, Mara. Your dress is magnificent,” Sonia replied. “You look like a real Spanish Condesa in those robes. It’s truly breathtaking.”
Philippe observed the two women with satisfaction. “Henry, your ward’s attire is both elegant and appropriately restrictive. You have outdone yourself.”
Henry nodded, pleased. “Thank you, Philippe. My gözde embodies the essence of an odalisque tonight. And Mara’s dress—what a masterpiece of opulence and restraint.”
Mara curtsied to Henry, then turned to Philippe. “Thank you, Sir. I am honored to wear such a beautiful dress.”
Philippe smiled warmly. “You wear it well, Mara. Tonight, you are my Konstanze, a true vision of beauty and grace.”
As the group was still exchanging pleasantries, the first bell rang, signaling the opening of the auditorium doors. Philippe guided them to their box, where they found two seats and two kneeling pads with locking connectors for the women. The men secured the women to their pads, making sure they were settled for the performance. They exchanged a few words until the overture began.
The opera started with a burst of vibrant colors and music. Konstanze appeared in a lavish emerald green dress, richly embroidered with gold and pearls. Her bodice was tightly laced, and her arms were encased in long sleeves that ended in cuffs. Her skirt was heavy and layered, clearly restricting her movement. Blondchen, her maid, wore a similarly confining blue outfit with silver adornments. Both costumes highlighted the women’s lack of freedom.
The men on stage were dressed in luxurious fabrics that symbolized power. Bassa Selim, the Pasha, wore deep red robes trimmed with gold, his turban adorned with a ruby. His commanding presence stood in stark contrast to the women’s bondage. Tension built as Konstanze and Blondchen struggled with their captivity, their restricted movements contrasting with the soaring defiance in their voices. The music swelled with emotion, and the first act ended with Konstanze’s powerful aria, “Ach, ich liebte, war so glücklich,” leaving the audience in awe.
During intermission, Philippe and Henry unlocked their wards and helped them to their feet. They led the women into the grand foyer, where Philippe considered getting snacks and wine for the group, and perhaps a feed bag for Mara. They found a free table by a bar, and Henry quickly locked Sonia to the ring at the center, using the chain from her collar. This left her standing at attention with her hands manacled behind her back. Philippe, on the other hand, just used his cellphone to configure Mara’s iGuardian to keep her in place.
Just as the men were about to leave, Henry noticed a woman moving awkwardly through the crowd. Something about her stood out, and as he looked closer, he realized why. She was clearly without corset, her heels were barely six centimeters high, and her face, half visible under an undecorated Jinshuwan, was shockingly bare of makeup. Her lack of proper attire made Henry instantly suspicious.
The woman was trailing behind her guardian, struggling to keep up. Her guardian was in a simple business suit instead of a proper dinner suit, and his shoes scuffed—clearly out of place among the polished evening wear of the other guardians. Even more troubling, the man didn’t offer her an arm or hand for support, despite her obvious struggle. A proper guardian would never be so neglectful; they always kept a watchful eye on their wards, assisting as needed.
The scene sent a wave of unease through Henry. He remembered the recent attack at the Green Gala by the Freeborn. The exact origin of that group was unknown, but they were seen as dangerous terrorists, radicals known for their use of breather masks to avoid infection with LASS-VASH-2024, who claimed that virus was brainwashing people, and who aimed to restore the chaotic pre-Change world. His eyes narrowed, and he pointed the couple out to Philippe.
“Something’s off with them,” Henry murmured. “Look at her—no corset, no makeup. And him… that suit? It doesn’t fit this setting. He’s not even paying attention to her.”
Philippe’s gaze followed Henry’s direction. His expression tightened as he quickly took action. “You’re right. This doesn’t look right at all.”
Philippe seemed to come to the same conclusion as Henry. He unlocked Mara’s iGuardian and turned to Henry. “Free Sonia. I’ll take the women back to our booth. You alert security.”
Henry swiftly unlocked Sonia’s restraints, and Philippe led her and Mara away. With Sonia cared for, Henry pulled out his cellphone, dialing for help as he began to follow the suspicious pair at a safe distance.
Henry reported location and cause, keeping his voice low, kept updating the other side while he casually strolled after the pair. “A man and a woman, both underdressed for the event. I think they’re Freeborn.” As he trailed them, he noticed more people scattered throughout the crowd, similarly out of place. He reported his observations to the security team on the other end of the line.
Then, chaos erupted. Several of the Freeborn suddenly moved with purpose, grabbing women from the crowd, trying to pull them to the exits. Two of the Freeborn pulled handguns, brandishing them at the terrified guests. Screams broke out as the crowd recoiled, fear spreading through the foyer.
But just as quickly as it began, it ended. A Grenadier SWAT team, alerted by Henry, stormed in from the front and sides. The heavily armed troops team wasted no time. Each of the two gunmen was immediately swarmed by four grenadiers in full riot gear, and within seconds, the attackers were disarmed and pinned to the ground. The other would-be kidnappers were similarly overwhelmed by the fast-acting security forces, subdued before they could cause any real harm.
Henry stepped back, watching as the chaos was swiftly brought under control. The grenadiers moved efficiently, ensuring no harm came to the guests. Guardians rushed to the sides of their freed wards, helping them adjust their dresses and restraints, or guiding them toward the washrooms to freshen their makeup and calm their nerves.
No one was hurt, save for the two gunmen, who would likely be nursing broken ribs from the rough takedown. Theater Director Perroux soon appeared, calling the crowd to order. His calm voice echoed through the room, soothing the remaining unease.
“Ladies and gentlemen, please remain calm,” he said confidently. “The situation is under control. No one has been injured. The show will go on.”
Meanwhile, Philippe led Mara and Sonia into the opera box as quickly as their restraints allowed. Once inside, he closed and locked the door, then stood by, cellphone in hand, waiting for a message from Henry.
Sonia felt a twinge of worry, unsure what to do. She glanced at Mara, who stood beside her kneeling pad, poised and calm. Her curiosity got the better of her. She signed. Mara, how do you stay so composed? You never seem to falter.
Mara responded with calm, precise hand-dancing. Discipline is not a choice for this one, Sonia. It is perfection or correction, exactly as the iGuardian says.
Sonia, thankful for the distraction, signed back. Perfection or correction? What does that mean?
Mara’s expression softened as she explained. Philippe chose the iGuardian because this one used to push boundaries, always testing limits. She would try to twist situations to her own advantage. The iGuardian keeps her focused and makes sure she remains within her role and duties.
Sonia nodded thoughtfully, reflecting on her own experience. “When I became Henry’s ward, he took a similar approach. He put me in a chastity belt.” She paused, lost in thought. “To be honest, I asked for it at first because I felt insecure. But then I struggled with the loss of control. It felt too much, too harsh. But Henry was patient. Over time, I learned, and now I understand why he did it.”
Mara, noticing Sonia’s need for distraction, continued signing. It is not so different from what this one went through. Philippe knew this one needed something firm, something that would not bend to her will. The iGuardian reminds her of her responsibilities. It guides her, and corrects her when she steps out of line.
Sonia met Mara’s gaze, and a quiet understanding passed between them. “Henry was the same with me. His corrections felt harsh at first, but now I see they were acts of care. He shaped me into someone better. I’ve grown because of it.”
Mara agreed, signing carefully. Love is shown through the discipline that shapes us into our true selves, whether it comes from a guardian’s guidance or from something like the iGuardian.
