With the same flick of her blade, the woman slashed the front of Seraphina’s dress, the fabric parting like silk under the blade.
“What the hell—” Seraphina began, but the words caught in her throat as the woman yanked the ruined dress from her shoulders with startling strength. The bindings followed, then her undergarments, until she stood naked in the frigid air, goosebumps prickling her skin.
The woman stepped back, her sharp eyes raking over Seraphina’s frame. “Thin. Wild. Bad posture,” she muttered, half to herself. Reaching for a tape measure, she quickly took several measurements, her hands moving with dispassionate efficiency.
Seraphina glared at her, her face burning. “You could have asked, you know.”
The woman didn’t respond. She turned to a row of cupboards, throwing them open with a series of quick, practiced movements. From within, she pulled out a bundle of garments: a coarse slip, a corset in drab gray, a narrow underskirt, and a charcoal wool dress so stiff and scratchy it looked as though it might stand on its own. Next came a pair of woolen stockings, high-heeled boots, kid gloves, a detachable stiff white collar, and a plain apron.
“Here,” the woman barked, thrusting the pile toward Seraphina. “You dress. Now.”
Seraphina raised her chin, her arms crossed defiantly over her chest. “You expect me to wear that? You must be joking.”
The slap came so quickly Seraphina barely registered the motion. The woman’s hand cracked against her cheek, snapping her head to the side. Tears sprang to her eyes unbidden, more from shock than pain.
The woman’s voice, low and dangerous, cut through her stunned silence. “I did not ask for talk. I gave order. You dress, da?”
Seraphina turned back to face her, her lips trembling. “You can’t just—”
The second slap landed harder, from the opposite side, leaving both her cheeks stinging and her vision swimming.
“No talk,” the woman growled, leaning in close enough that Seraphina could feel her breath. “You are not here to talk. You are here to obey. Now dress.”
Tears slid down Seraphina’s face, but she said nothing. Her hands, trembling with cold and rage, reached for the slip. The scratchy woolen slip clung to Seraphina’s skin, its coarseness a constant reminder of her situation. She shivered as she pulled the stockings up her legs, the thick material promising some relief from the icy air of the reformatory. They reached mid-thigh, to be held snugly in place by garters attached to the corset waiting ominously nearby.
The maid sat her down on a chair, for the boots that came next—high, stiff, and gleaming black leather. The Russian maid crouched before her, her rough hands pulling the laces tight with merciless efficiency. Seraphina winced as her arches were forced into an unnatural curve, the five-inch heels angling her feet steeply. The snug leather left no room for her to adjust; every movement of her toes felt locked into the rigid structure of the boots. The maid’s cold gaze flicked up to meet Seraphina’s.
“Stand,” she ordered.
Seraphina obeyed reluctantly, wobbling slightly as the boots made balance a challenge. The maid clucked her tongue. “You learn soon,” she muttered before moving on to the corset.
The garment itself was simple in design, but its effects were anything but. The maid fastened it around Seraphina’s waist, tugging the laces in passes, once, twice, each pass stealing more air from her lungs. There was a brief pause before the third and final pass. The maid braced her foot against Seraphina’s back, yanking the laces with such force that Seraphina gasped, her knees threatening to buckle.
The maid secured the laces with a knot pressed flat by a screw nut, tightening it between two small washers before sealing it with a blob of crimson wax. “Temporary corset,” she said flatly. “Proper one comes after first week.”
Seraphina’s chest heaved, her breath shallow and fast. She felt lightheaded, her vision swimming for a moment before she steadied herself. But there was no reprieve—the kid gloves came next, the maid tugging them over her hands and buttoning them tightly with a small buttonhook. The snug leather hugged her fingers, leaving her hands useless for any delicate movement.
Then came the hobbling underskirt, hooked to the corset with small clasps. It narrowed her stride to mere inches, each step now a deliberate, shuffling motion. Petticoats followed, their weight pressing down on her hips, and then the woolen school dress. The fabric was rough against her skin, warm but unbearably coarse. The high detachable collar was wrapped around her neck with a small strap, forcing her head upward. Seraphina realized with dawning horror that she could no longer look down or even turn her head without immense effort.
Her hair was next. The maid’s fingers worked with brutal precision, pulling Seraphina’s locks into a painfully tight bun that left her scalp aching. A stiff bonnet was secured over her head, tied tightly under her chin and buttoned to the high collar. The final indignity left her head locked in place, unable to move even slightly.
When the maid stepped back to inspect her work, Seraphina stood swaddled in layers of coarse wool, her movements slow, her breath shallow, and her head forced to stare straight ahead. The maid gave a curt nod, her satisfaction evident.
“You go now,” she said, gesturing to the door.
The maid from earlier awaited her return, her expression as serene as if Seraphina were dressed for tea rather than a waking nightmare. Without a word, she turned and led Seraphina back through the echoing halls to Miss Blackthorn’s office.
The walk felt endless, each shuffle of her feet a struggle against the unyielding corset and skirt. By the time they arrived, Seraphina’s breaths were shallow and her resolve had worn thin. The office door opened, and Miss Blackthorn rose from her desk, her dark eyes assessing the figure before her.
She said nothing to Seraphina, addressing only the maid. “Has she been properly prepared?”
The maid nodded. “Oui, Miss Blackthorn. She is ready.”
“Good,” Miss Blackthorn said, her voice cold and precise. Her gaze flicked briefly to Seraphina, but she might as well have been inspecting a mannequin. “I will take her to the dormitory myself. Her training begins at dawn.”
Miss Blackthorn stopped before Seraphina, inspecting her closely, her dark eyes noting every tightened seam, every painfully straight line forced by the uniform. She finally nodded to Lady Thistledown. “Already much improved,” she said with clinical approval. “I assure you, Lady Thistledown, we will take good care of her and produce the results you desire within the allotted time.”
Seraphina’s lips parted, a retort rising before she could stop it. “I’m not—”
Miss Blackthorn moved with unsettling swiftness, closing the distance between them in an instant. From somewhere unseen, she had produced a short, cruel-looking riding crop. The leather tip pressed sharply into the delicate spot between Seraphina’s jaw and neck, tilting her head ever so slightly upward in painful compliance, straining against the collar and the bonnet’s fastening.
“As a rule,” Miss Blackthorn said, her voice soft but brimming with menace, “a young lady will speak only when spoken to. You would do well to take this rule to heart.”
The cold leather bit into her skin, and Seraphina swallowed hard, her defiance faltering under the weight of Miss Blackthorn’s unrelenting gaze. She clenched her teeth, holding back the sharp words she so desperately wanted to hurl, and instead offered the smallest nod she could manage under the circumstances.
Satisfied, Miss Blackthorn withdrew the crop and turned back to Lady Thistledown, her demeanor reverting to its cold professionalism.
Lady Thistledown smiled, her earlier tension melting away. “I am confident she is in capable hands, Miss Blackthorn. I have no doubt she will become the refined young lady we both know she can be.”
She gathered her cloak, casting a final glance at Seraphina. “Goodbye, my dear. I look forward to seeing your progress.”
The door shut behind her with a heavy finality, leaving Seraphina and Miss Blackthorn alone in the suffocating silence of the office.
Miss Blackthorn moved back to her desk, picking up a ledger and inspecting it briefly. Without looking at Seraphina, she said, “Come.”
Seraphina obeyed reluctantly, shuffling behind the governess as she led her down a narrow, dimly lit corridor. The tight confines of her uniform made every step laborious, the boots forcing her feet into an unnaturally rapid rhythm of mincing steps, the hobbling skirt keeping her stride to mere inches. She was already sweating despite the chill of the building, her skin chafing against the coarse wool of the dress.
They stopped at a plain wooden door near the end of the corridor. Miss Blackthorn unlocked it and pushed it open, revealing a small, sparsely furnished room. Two narrow beds were positioned against opposite walls, each with a simple trunk at the foot. A single window high on the far wall let in a sliver of gray light.
Inside, a young woman sat on one of the beds, her hands folded primly in her lap. Her uniform was identical to Seraphina’s, though she wore it with practiced ease. Her hair was coiled and hidden neatly into a severe bun with a single honey-blonde strain escaping, and her pale blue eyes fixed on Seraphina with an expression of mild curiosity.
“This is where you will stay,” Miss Blackthorn said. “You will share this room with Miss Penelope Fairfax. She has been with us for six months and will serve as an example of proper behavior. Is that understood?”
Seraphina forced herself to nod, the collar biting into her throat as she did. Miss Blackthorn turned to Penelope.
“Miss Fairfax, this is Miss Seraphina Arabella Lockewood. See to it that she learns our ways quickly.”
Penelope rose gracefully, her movements smooth despite the restrictions of her uniform. “Yes, Miss Blackthorn.”
Miss Blackthorn cast one final, assessing glance at Seraphina before stepping out and shutting the door behind her. The sound of the lock clicking echoed in the small room.
Penelope offered a faint, polite smile. “Welcome to Loch Thorne, Seraphina,” she said, her voice lilting with an upper-class accent. “I imagine you’ll find things quite… different here.”
Seraphina sat heavily on her bed, the stiff corset forcing her to remain upright even in her exhaustion. “Different,” she muttered, her voice low with suppressed rage. “That’s one way to put it.”
Penelope’s smile didn’t falter. “Best to keep that to yourself,” she advised, her tone calm but firm. “Miss Blackthorn has a way of… correcting those who speak out of turn.”
Seraphina looked away, her jaw tight. She had no intention of playing by their rules, but for now, she would bide her time.
Loch Thorne, Evening# Sitting on the edge of the narrow bed, Seraphina fumbled uselessly at the buttons on her wrists. The tiny fastenings were impossible to grip, slipping from her gloved grasp every time she tried to pull at them.
“Bloody hell,” she muttered under her breath, her frustration bubbling over. Her fingers tugged at the gloves again, desperate for even the smallest relief.
Across the room, Penelope watched her impassively from her own bed, her hands folded neatly in her lap. “Don’t,” she said, her voice calm but with an edge of warning.
Seraphina’s head snapped up—or rather, tried to. The stiff collar and bonnet locked her head in place, forcing her to tilt her entire torso to meet Penelope’s gaze. “Don’t what?” she snapped.
“Don’t try to upset your uniform,” Penelope said simply, her tone patient as though addressing a stubborn child. “If you aren’t properly dressed for the dinner inspection, you’ll fail it. That means no meal and a correction.”
“Correction?” Seraphina scoffed, though her chest tightened at the word. “What’s that supposed to mean? Another slap, or do they have something worse in store?”
Penelope’s expression didn’t waver. “Worse. You’ll desperately want to avoid it. Trust me.”
Seraphina let out a string of curses under her breath, some in English, others in languages she’d learned in India. Her fingers almost curled into fists, until the smooth leather stopped her, creaking. She looked down at herself, and felt the high collar biting into her neck, the hobbling skirt locking her legs into short, shuffling steps, the gloves that rendered her hands nearly useless. Everything about her current state screamed restraint.
She stood, the stiff petticoats rustling as she moved, and shuffled toward the trunk at the foot of her bed. Her boots pinched with every step, the high heels forcing her to place each foot down carefully. Leaning over was impossible with the corset digging into her ribs, and she was forced to awkwardly kneel to examine the trunk. She fumbled at the latch, but her gloved fingers couldn’t grip it properly. Frustrated, she got back onto her heels and turned herself to look around the room.
The furnishings were sparse and cold, the walls painted in dull, uninspiring tones. The single window above the far wall let in a gray, watery light, but it was set so high that she had no chance of reaching it, especially not in her current outfit. She spotted another door on Penelope’s side of the room and shuffled toward it, her movements slow and jerky.
The door led to a small lavatory. A washbasin with a cracked porcelain edge, a simple loo, and a vanity stood crammed into the space. Another high window let in faint light, but like the one in the main room, it was unreachable. Seraphina ran her gloved hands along the edge of the vanity, searching for something—anything—that might help her remove her gloves, her collar, anything. But the buttons on her gloves were too small, the corset too tight, the collar too immovable. Her restricted range of motion made it impossible to even reach behind her back to fiddle with the buttons on the dress or her skirts.
She returned to the main room, silently fighting against the restrictions of her dress. Penelope’s voice broke the silence. “It’s meant to be like this.”
“What?” Seraphina snapped, her hands trembling with frustration as she gave up on the collar and sat heavily on the bed.
“The uniform,” Penelope said, her voice quiet. “It’s… portable bondage. Everything about it is designed to keep you in line. You’ll find no relief from it unless they allow it.”
Seraphina glared at her, anger and helplessness churning in her chest. “What the hell kind of place is this?”
Penelope tilted her head slightly, her bun pulling tightly against her scalp. “The One where they store you, until you manage to present yourself in a way that a man will marry you and take you with him.”
Seraphina’s lips pressed into a thin line. For the first time in her life, she felt entirely trapped—not just physically, but by the sheer weight of the institution around her. She glanced toward the locked door and swallowed hard.
Seraphina sat down again on the edge of the bed, fidgeting against her restrictions. She glared at Penelope, who remained the picture of calm composure, hands folded neatly in her lap as if she had been born into this peculiar nightmare.
“Well?” Seraphina demanded. “What’s the game here? What are the rules of this… charming establishment?”
Penelope raised an eyebrow, her lips twitching with the faintest hint of amusement. “The rules are simple. First and foremost: always be pretty and dainty. Miss Blackthorn believes a proper woman must be presentable and composed at all times.”
“Pretty and dainty,” Seraphina repeated, sarcastically. “How delightful.”
“That means,” Penelope continued, undeterred, “you will greet others politely, always with a curtsy. You will say thank you for everything you receive—whether it’s a gift or a punishment. And yes, with a curtsy.”
Seraphina let out a bitter laugh. “Thank you for beating me? For starving me? What else?”
Penelope’s calm gaze never wavered. “You are to be seen, not heard. Do not speak unless spoken to, and always be polite. And whatever you do, don’t cuss.”
“What are they going to do, wash my mouth with soap?” Seraphina sneered.
“That, or the gag,” Penelope said lightly. “Or the brank.”
“The brank?” Seraphina repeated, her brows furrowing. “What in God’s name is that?”
Penelope hesitated for a moment before explaining. “It’s… a metal gag. A punishment for particularly foul or defiant language. It locks over your head, and the gag is inserted into your mouth. Uncomfortable, to say the least.”
Seraphina blinked, the weight of Penelope’s words sinking in like a stone. She swallowed hard, but her defiance flared again. “They’re not going to break me with some ridiculous gag. I’ll manage.”
Penelope’s face softened, almost pitying. “There’s more. You’ll be inspected before every meal. Your uniform, posture, and demeanor must be impeccable. If you fail, you don’t eat.”
Seraphina stiffened. “What? They starve us?”
“And you’ll receive a correction,” Penelope added. “That’s for any infractions, not just meals. If your uniform is improper, your dress isn’t pristine, or you disobey… corrections follow.”
Seraphina’s mind raced, the unfamiliar terminology grating against her pride. “Corrections,” she muttered. “What are those? Whippings?”
Penelope sighed. “Not usually. Open defiance or severe infractions might earn a whipping, but most corrections are… restrictive.” She gestured vaguely at Seraphina’s uniform. “Improper dress earns correction dress. And trust me, it can always get worse.”
Seraphina frowned, tugging at the stiff collar around her neck. “Worse than this?” she scoffed. “What is this even supposed to be?”
“That,” Penelope said with a faint smile, “is the beginner uniform.”
Seraphina’s stomach twisted. The scratchy wool, the unyielding corset, the hobbling skirt, the immovable collar, the snug gloves that left her fingers useless—all of it was just the beginning? She shifted uncomfortably on the bed, the tight leather boots digging into her arches, her body aching from the constant strain.
“This place,” Seraphina said slowly, her voice tinged with incredulity, “isn’t just about rules. It’s a bloody prison.”
Penelope nodded, her expression turning somber. “It’s a reformatory. And they’ll reform you, one way or another. The sooner you learn the rules and follow them, the easier it’ll be.”
Seraphina stared at her, the fire in her chest dimming into something colder and sharper: determination. “We’ll see about that,” she muttered.
“What else do we do? Sit here in our prison cell, in silence?” Seraphina snapped in frustration.
“We have classes,” Penelope replied, her tone steady but without much enthusiasm. “Etiquette, conversation in English and French, dance, deportment, calligraphy, literature, needlework, and religion.”
“Nothing useful?” Seraphina scoffed. “And how am I supposed to do calligraphy or needlework with these?” She held up her gloved hands, the snug leather creaking with the movement. “I can barely grip my own skirts.”
“You will learn,” Penelope said, her expression unreadable. “We all do.”
Before Seraphina could fire back another complaint, the sound of a key turning in the lock echoed down the corridor. Penelope’s demeanor shifted immediately, her posture snapping into rigid perfection. She lifted a single finger to her lips, silencing Seraphina with an urgent, “Ssssh.”
The door swung open, and Miss Blackthorn’s dark silhouette appeared in the corridor. Without hesitation, Penelope shuffled out of the room, her head held high, her steps small and precise. Seraphina hesitated but followed, mimicking the shuffling motion and finding it maddeningly slow. Outside, all the girls stood at attention next to their doors, a silent line of identical figures in scratchy gray uniforms, their faces turned forward, their hands folded neatly at their waists.
Miss Blackthorn moved down the corridor with the precision of a general inspecting her troops. She stopped at each girl, her dark eyes sweeping over every detail of their appearance. “Dinner,” she said curtly to one. “Dinner,” to another. At the third, she paused, her gaze narrowing. “Your makeup is incorrect,” she said icily. “To correction.” The girl’s face fell, but she curtsied, “Thank you, Miss Blackthorn,” and turned toward the end of the hall without a word.
Seraphina stiffened as Miss Blackthorn approached her. She felt the governess’s eyes rake over her, lingering on her stiff collar, her perfectly buttoned gloves, and the polished leather of her boots. The silence stretched unbearably before Miss Blackthorn finally said, “Dinner.” She moved on without another glance, and Seraphina exhaled shakily.
When the inspection was complete, the girls began to shuffle in pairs down the corridor. Seraphina fell into step next to Penelope, her hobbling skirt and high heels forcing her into the same maddeningly short strides as the others.
The mess hall was as austere as the rest of the reformatory—long rows of plain wooden tables and benches, lit by flickering gas lamps. They took their seats without a word, their movements silent and orderly. Miss Blackthorn stood at the head of the hall, at the raised teachers table, her mere presence silencing even the faintest rustle of fabric. At her gesture, one girl rose from her seat, folded her hands, and began to pray.
“Bless us, O Lord, for these Thy gifts which we are about to receive,” she said, her voice clear and steady. The rest of the hall joined her in unison: “Amen.”
As soon as the prayer ended, the girls began to eat. The food was simple but surprisingly well-prepared—for English cuisine, at least. Roast beef, boiled potatoes, and steamed carrots sat on the plate before Seraphina, but the mere sight of it made her stomach twist. After years of flavorful, spiced Indian food, the blandness was unbearable. Not that it mattered; her corset restricted her appetite to mere nibbles anyway.
Eating proved to be its own ordeal. The gloves, snug and unyielding, made gripping utensils a clumsy struggle. Each movement required exaggerated care, and the rigid collar kept her head locked upright, forcing her to rely on her peripheral vision to see her plate.
Dinner was silent, save for the faint clinking of utensils. When the meal ended, Miss Blackthorn announced the evening options. “You may walk the grounds, read in the library, visit the chapel, or listen to Mademoiselle Artois reading in French. Choose wisely.”
Seraphina didn’t hesitate. She shuffled toward the exit, craving fresh air more than anything else. The grounds were enclosed on three sides by the looming reformatory, the fourth bordered by a tall stone wall. Within the yard was a small garden, its flowerbeds barren in the cold Scottish winter, some evergreen hedges marking the ways. The air was sharp and crisp, biting at her cheeks, but it was a welcome change from the stifling indoors.
She moved slowly, the hobbling skirt and high heels turning every step into an effort. Her vision remained restricted by the bonnet and collar, forcing her to look only forward. The limited view was frustrating, but the cold air soothed her raw nerves. For the first time that day, she felt a semblance of peace—though it was a fragile thing, overshadowed by the looming walls and the constant weight of her bindings.
Her breath puffed in the cold air as she shuffled along the paved paths, carefully staying on them to prevent sinking into the ground with the high heels of her boots. She held her arms folded neatly as she saw the other girls do, because even this small act of freedom was monitored. She couldn’t shake the oppressive sense of control that hung over every corner of this place, but for now, she let the fresh air fill her lungs as much as the corset allowed.
As the sun dipped below the horizon, the sharp clang of a bell echoed across the grounds, its metallic tone summoning the girls back indoors. Seraphina shuffled along with the rest, her steps constrained by the hobbling skirt and punishing heels. The brisk evening air gave way to the building’s oppressive chill and institutional scent.
Once back in their room, Penelope settled onto her bed with the practiced ease of routine. Seraphina remained standing, the rigid corset and stiff uniform refusing her any other option. Moments later, the door opened, and a robust maid stepped inside. She was a stout, ruddy-cheeked woman with arms like a blacksmith’s and a thick braid of dark hair coiled atop her head. Her accent was heavy, her words rolling like the low rumble of distant thunder.
“Aye, lassies,” she said, her tone brisk but not unkind. She turned to Seraphina. “I’m Morag, yer maid. I’ll keep ye in line, friendly-like, but mind this—there’ll be no tolerance fer unladylike carryin’ on.” She nodded firmly before adding, “Let’s be gettin’ ye ready fer bed, eh? Miss Blackthorn’ll have my head if yer late to sleep.”
Seraphina didn’t move, watching warily as Morag approached Penelope first. With quick, practiced motions, she unbuttoned Penelope’s gloves and, breaking the seal and losening the washers, unlaced her corset. Penelope exhaled softly, relief flickering across her features as she stepped out of the restrictive garment. “Yer turn next, new one,” Morag said, jerking her chin toward Seraphina.
The relief of being unbound from her corset was almost dizzying. Seraphina sighed as the laces came loose, the oppressive pressure on her ribs easing. Her gloves were removed with the aid of a buttonhook, and the hobbling skirt and stockings followed. She flexed her aching feet, marveling at the freedom, brief as it was.
“Off tae wash yerself, lass,” Morag ordered, nodding toward the door. “Clean yer face proper-like. No makeup left, mind ye.”
Seraphina complied, the cold water from the washbasin shocking against her skin. She scrubbed away the powder and rouge, her face left raw and chilled. When she returned, Morag had laid out her nightwear, and Seraphina’s stomach sank.
Night mittens were first, heavy padded coverings that curled her fingers into useless balls. Morag secured them tightly, buckling the straps with practiced efficiency. Next came the night corset, looser than the day version but longer, extending from her knees to her overbust. Morag laced it in two passes, humming softly under her breath as she pulled the laces taut.
“Ye’ll get used tae it,” she said as she knotted the laces and sealed the knot with the screw and the washers, and a final small dab of wax. “This one’s nothin’ compared tae yer trainin’ corset.”
Seraphina scowled but said nothing. She could feel the tension in the stays already making her movements slow and deliberate. The sleeping heels came next—shoes designed with no actual heels, forcing her feet into the same arched position as her day boots. Walking in them was impossible, not that the nightgown would allow much movement.
The long sack-like nightgown enveloped her completely, its narrow cut preventing her legs parting much even without the corset. Morag finished with a snug nightcap, tucking all of Seraphina’s hair inside before tying it securely under her chin.
Finally, she guided Seraphina to bed, placing her mittened hands on top of the heavy wool blanket before tucking it so tightly around her that Seraphina could barely breathe. “There now,” Morag said, stepping back to inspect her work. “Warm as a bairn in swaddlin’, aye?”
Warm wasn’t the word Seraphina would have chosen. She could hardly move. The corset kept her from turning, the mittens rendered her hands useless, and the heels ensured she couldn’t walk even if she got free.
Across the room, Penelope was already curled under her own cover, pliant and serene, her breath evening out in mere moments. Seraphina lay awake, every fiber of her body aching in protest. Sleep felt impossible, but exhaustion eventually overtook her in the small hours of the night.
Loch Thorne, Morning# The wake-up call came long before dawn, another sharp bell that jolted her from restless sleep. Morag returned, just as robust and brisk as the night before. Seraphina blinked groggily, her body stiff and sore from the unyielding corset and tucked-in covers.
“Up we go,” Morag said, hauling Seraphina upright with little ceremony. The sleeping heels and nightgown were removed, the mittens and the laces of her corset undone, until she was stark naked. Freedom was fleeting; the day uniform awaited: Slip and stockings went on first.
Morag laced her into her day corset, first pass. Stockings and boots followed, the heels just as steep and unrelenting as yesterday. Seraphina was sent to wash and apply her makeup, her gloves buttoned back on once she returned.
Penelope inspected Seraphina’s makeup with a critical eye, her own perfectly done. “A bit more rouge,” she said softly, dabbing at Seraphina’s cheeks with a practiced hand. “Miss Blackthorn will notice otherwise.”
Seraphina barely had time to adjust before Morag stepped in, her sturdy hands moving with brisk efficiency as she reached for the corset laces. “Time tae tighten these, lass,” she said, giving Seraphina a pointed look.
Seraphina stiffened, her already constricted ribs protesting. “I thought it was tight enough already,” she muttered carefully, biting back the sharper edge of her tone.
Morag chuckled, the sound deep and knowing. “Ach, tight enough fer a novice, maybe, but no’ fer inspection. Ye’ll handle it like a lady, now—silent and wi’ a smile.”
Before Seraphina could respond, Morag tugged the laces again, pulling them tighter in a second pass, and then in a third. The corset cinched in further, pressing Seraphina’s waist into a smaller curve, her breath growing shorter with each pass. She swallowed her protest, the corners of her lips twitching into a semblance of a smile despite the discomfort.
“Guid,” Morag said with a nod, securing the corset again with screw and washers, and sealing it with wax. “Discipline’s a kindness, ye ken. Ye’ll see it fer yerself someday.”
Seraphina said nothing, focusing instead on not swooning as the corset settled into its final, unyielding shape. Morag swiftly layered the underskirt, petticoats, and stiff woolen dress over the corset, each piece adding weight and restriction to the ensemble. The bonnet came last, its buttons locking her head upright once more.
By the time Morag stepped back, the uniform was complete, every detail precise. Seraphina felt as tightly packaged as she had the day before, the discipline etched into every line of her silhouette. Morag offered an approving nod before turning to Penelope.
“Ready fer inspection, the both o’ ye,” she said, ushering them toward the door. “Now off wi’ ye—an’ dinnae forget that smile, lass.”
Miss Blackthorn’s inspection was as exacting as ever, she moved through the line of girls with her unyielding gaze, her sharp eyes scanning every detail. When she reached Seraphina, her lips pressed into a thin line. Seraphina stood rigid, her hands folded at her waist, her face blank as the governess’s eyes scanned her from head to toe.
“Passable,” Miss Blackthorn said coldly. “Though your makeup requires improvement. See that it is corrected tomorrow.”
Seraphina bit the inside of her cheek but curtsied, murmuring, “Thank you, Miss Blackthorn.”
The girls shuffled in pairs to the mess hall, the procession silent. Breakfast was much like dinner: bland, unseasoned food that Seraphina couldn’t stomach in her corset, eaten in silence and with great difficulty due to her gloves. By the time the meal ended, her frustration simmered, but she could do nothing except shuffle out with the others.
The day’s first class was French. The girls sat in wooden benches, their postures dictated by the unyielding stays of their corsets. The teacher, Mademoiselle Vivienne Artois, delivered her lecture with clipped impatience, correcting any misstep in pronunciation with a sharp glare and an even sharper tongue.
When called upon, each girl was required to rise, step out from the bench, and deliver her answer before sitting again. Seraphina soon found the process exhausting; the combination of the hobbling skirt and tightly laced corset turned every movement into a calculated ordeal. By the time the lesson ended, her legs ached, and her breathing was shallow.
Calligraphy followed. Mr. Edward Penbridge, with his kind face and quiet manner, was a welcome change from the previous hour’s tension. He demonstrated elegant strokes on the board, his movements fluid and precise. “Grace,” he said softly, “is as much in your writing as in your posture.”
Taking notes, however, proved challenging. Seraphina’s gloves, snug and stiff, made gripping the pen awkward. She struggled to keep her strokes smooth, the ink smudging as her hand slipped across the page. Penelope leaned toward her and whispered, “Mind your gloves. They must stay clean at all times.”
Seraphina frowned but nodded, focusing harder. Yet, despite her efforts, a smudge of ink spread across the pale leather of her glove, unmistakable.
Mr. Penbridge approached and tutted softly, shaking his head. “Miss Lockewood,” he said, his tone gentle but firm, “what is done is done. The correction will help you to remember for next time. Report to Miss Blackthorn after class.”
Her stomach twisted at the words. She tried to protest, but his kind expression remained unmoved. “Go on,” he said, and she nodded reluctantly.
The trek to Miss Blackthorn’s office was the longest journey Seraphina could remember, though it was only a few corridors away. Her heart pounded against the confines of her corset, each breath shallow and tight. She had roamed jungles, barefoot and fearless, chased off panthers with little more than instinct and a blade. Yet here, surrounded by cold stone and stifling uniforms, she felt something alien creeping into her chest: fear.
She knocked on the door with her mittened hand, the sound faint but crisp in the stillness. From within, Miss Blackthorn’s voice rang out, calm and commanding.
“Enter.”
Seraphina straightened her shoulders, gathering what composure she could under the circumstances. She would not be cowed by an old, unmarried matron running a glorified prison for young women in the frigid north of the British Isles. With a deliberate movement, she opened the door and stepped inside, her chin high and her steps as poised and regal as the restricting uniform would allow.
Miss Blackthorn sat behind her desk, her dark eyes cold and assessing. Seraphina stopped a few paces before her and curtsied just enough to satisfy decorum. “Miss Blackthorn,” she began, her tone measured, “Mr. Penbridge asked me to report to you on account of this.” She lifted her gloved hand, the ink smudge dark against the pale leather. “It seems unreasonable to expect gloves to remain clean when performing calligraphy in gloves such as these.”
Miss Blackthorn’s lips pressed into a thin line. She rose from her chair, her corseted figure a striking pillar of authority. “The punishment for soiled gloves is three on the open hand.”
Seraphina stiffened but held her ground. “Miss Blackthorn,” she said, her voice firm yet polite, “I do not believe that, as a lady, I am meant to work with tools that are unsuitable for the purpose. Surely there must be gloves designed for such tasks, ones that allow for calligraphy without the inevitable risk of…”
“Enough.” Miss Blackthorn’s voice cut through the air like a blade. She stepped forward, her dark gaze fixed on Seraphina’s face. “You will learn to handle the tools you are given and still be a lady, always. There are no exceptions.”
Seraphina’s jaw tightened as she curtsied again, this time slower, deliberate. “As you say, Miss Blackthorn,” she replied, her voice steady but with a defiant edge. Inside, her resolve hardened. She had tried to reason with this woman, to work within her rigid framework, but it was clear there would be no compromise.
This meant war.
Miss Blackthorn rang a small silver bell, its sharp tone summoning a maid. As the maid entered, Miss Blackthorn turned to Seraphina with an air of cold efficiency. Taking a buttonhook from her desk, she began unfastening the buttons on Seraphina’s soiled gloves, her movements precise and almost mechanical. Once removed, she handed the gloves to the waiting maid.
“Fetch a fresh pair,” Miss Blackthorn ordered. The maid curtsied and left the room.
Miss Blackthorn’s sharp gaze returned to Seraphina. “Extend your hand.”
Seraphina’s heart pounded, but she refused to let her fear show. With a deep breath to steady herself, she stretched her hand forward, the fingers trembling only slightly. Miss Blackthorn picked up a slender willow cane from her desk and positioned it over Seraphina’s palm.
The first strike came swiftly, a sharp sting radiating through her hand.
“One,” Seraphina counted clearly, her voice steady. “Thank you, Miss Blackthorn.”
The second landed, sharper than the first, and her palm burned with pain.
“Two,” she said, her voice unwavering. “Thank you, Miss Blackthorn.”
The third strike bit cruelly against her skin, her fingers instinctively twitching from the sting.
“Three,” she finished, her voice even. “Thank you, Miss Blackthorn.”
Tears pricked at the edges of her vision, but she held them back, forcing her mind to another place. She remembered a time in the jungle when she had stepped barefoot onto a thorny vine, its sharp barbs slicing deep into her skin. Raji had helped her pull them out, one by one, while she had gritted her teeth and bit back cries of pain. This was nothing compared to that, she told herself.
The maid returned, a pristine pair of gloves folded neatly on a silver tray. Miss Blackthorn took them, slipping them over Seraphina’s hands with a measured care that contrasted sharply with the punishment she had just delivered. She fastened each button with the buttonhook, ensuring every detail was perfect before stepping back.
“You will take more care to present yourself as a lady at all times,” Miss Blackthorn said, her tone clipped.
“Of course, Miss Blackthorn,” Seraphina replied, curtsying deeply. Her lips curved into a polite smile, though her eyes betrayed nothing but icy defiance.
“Return to class.”
Seraphina curtsied again and turned, moving toward the door with a poise that could rival royalty. She left the office, her steps slow and measured, every inch of her outward appearance regal. Inside, however, her thoughts simmered with violent fantasies that she entertained in exquisite detail.
At lunch, the quiet hum of silverware against plates filled the mess hall. Seraphina sat stiffly, her corset pressing relentlessly against her ribs, her gloved hands gripping her utensils with precision. As the meal continued, her fingers worked deftly, guiding the blade of her knife to slip between the cuff of her blouse and her fresh glove. Her movements were deliberate, subtle enough to escape notice.
The blade pressed lightly against her skin—not with intent to harm but as a reminder that even in this prison, she could still find ways to reclaim a sliver of control.
Loch Thorne, first week# The days at Loch Thorne passed with a grinding monotony. Seraphina fell into the rigid schedule of classes, inspections, and mealtimes, her corset shaping both her posture and her movements into the perfect image of Victorian propriety. Her nights were no better—bound in night stays that stretched from her knees to her overbust, her hands useless in mittens, and her legs immobilized by her sack-like nightgown. She had tested the limits of her night mittens and sleeping heels but quickly realized their design left her utterly helpless. Escape during the night was impossible.
During the brief moments between one corset and the next, while Morag bustled around preparing her next layer of restraint, Seraphina felt the closest thing to freedom. These windows were fleeting, lasting mere minutes, but they reminded her that her body was still her own, even if the institution sought to control it completely. Yet, of all the figures at Loch Thorne, Morag earned her respect, if not affection. The Scottish maid’s brusque kindness and hard-won patience did not deserve the violence brewing inside Seraphina. No, Morag would not be the target of her rebellion.
Seraphina’s mind turned constantly to the problem of her gloves. The kid leather bound her hands almost as surely as her night mittens, rendering anything requiring fine dexterity a challenge. She knew she would need to free her hands first, and then her corset and underskirt, to move with any measure of independence. The woolen dress, while heavy and coarse, was tolerable in the freezing Scottish climate, and the heels and petticoats served to keep her skirts from dragging in the mud.
So, she waited. She observed. Every buttonhook, pin, and stray tool became a potential means of escape. She managed to slip a buttonhook into the stuffing of her mattress during one of Morag’s lacing sessions, where it rested next to the knife. If she could get her hands on a hat pin, it would be invaluable—but the only proper hat pins she had seen belonged to Mrs. Everstone, her stern and humorless Etiquette teacher. Seraphina would need to watch carefully for an opportunity to acquire one without drawing suspicion.
Outwardly, Seraphina was a model of Victorian ladyship. She curtsied with perfect grace, her makeup flawless, her posture immaculate. She responded with soft politeness, thanked her instructors with demure bows of her head, and never gave a hint of defiance in her tone. But her eyes, cold and sharp, betrayed none of the submission her body language suggested. Beneath the surface, she was a coiled spring, waiting, watching, planning.
Miss Blackthorn noticed.
Years of experience with wayward girls had taught her to recognize rebellion in all its forms. Most girls fought openly, raging against their restraints until they were broken into meek submission. But Seraphina presented no such outward struggle. Her pliancy was perfect—too perfect. There was no outburst, no tantrum, no crisis that could be thwarted to bring about the final breaking point. Her obedience felt like a veneer, thin and calculated, masking something far more dangerous.
Miss Blackthorn studied her with the precision of a predator sizing up its prey. Seraphina was not a tame cat, nor a girl who had been broken into compliance. She was a tigress, lying in wait, her sharp mind calculating every step, her claws ready to strike when the moment came. She had seen this before in girls who thought themselves clever, but none quite like Seraphina. The fire in her eyes, the silence in her rebellion—it was disquieting.
She would not let her guard down. Seraphina was not just obstinate; she bore all the hallmarks of true danger, and Miss Blackthorn was determined to keep her from turning her plans into action.
Loch Thorne, two months later# The morning began with a familiar rhythm: inspections, classes, and the monotonous grind of the reformatory. Seraphina’s outward demeanor was flawless as always, her curtsies deep and graceful, her posture impeccable, and her words soft and polite. Inside, however, her mind churned with plans and calculations. Over two months, she had quietly amassed an arsenal of small, useful tools—knives, hatpins, buttonhooks, and anything else she could acquire. She stashed them carefully, moving items from her mattress to the solarium, the garden, and other discreet places unlikely to be traced back to her. It was a delicate game, and she played it with patience.
The arrival of a visitor disrupted the usual routine. A coach pulled up to the loch, its black exterior gleaming in the weak Scottish sunlight. From it emerged a tall man in his late thirties, his posture as straight as the line of his pressed military coat. Major Sebastian Hartwell carried himself with the quiet authority of a man accustomed to command. His dark hair was streaked with silver at the temples, and his mustache was immaculately groomed. A sharp, angled jaw and weathered complexion spoke of years spent in the colonies, his piercing blue eyes scanning his surroundings with practiced precision.
Major Hartwell stepped into the boat waiting at the pier, his polished boots clicking softly against the wood. The oarsman rowed him across the loch, the rhythmic sound of the oars breaking the stillness. Upon arriving at the reformatory, he was greeted with the restrained decorum reserved for visitors. His purpose was clear: to see his younger sister, Elizabeth Hartwell, one of the girls under Miss Blackthorn’s strict supervision.
The meeting was brief but tense. Elizabeth, pale and nervous, was summoned to the parlor, where Major Hartwell delivered disturbing news from home. After only an hour, it was decided—Elizabeth would leave the reformatory immediately, her presence required by her family. The announcement caused a ripple of speculation among the girls, though none dared voice it aloud.
For Seraphina, the commotion presented an opportunity. She slipped away unnoticed, making her way to one of her hidden stashes. In the small, rarely-used solarium, she retrieved a knife she had hidden behind a loose stone in the wall. With practiced efficiency, she sliced through the tight leather of her gloves, freeing her hands. She moved quickly, cutting through the fabric of her hobble skirt to give herself a wider range of movement. The bonnet and the collar, which locked her head upright, was the next to go, the blade making short work of it.
Her corset, unfortunately, had to stay—without it, her dress would not fit, and removing it would cost her precious time. Likewise, the high-heeled boots were necessary; without them, her skirts would trip her, and she’d be unable to walk. She adjusted what remained of her attire and slipped silently out of the solarium with quick movements.
Reaching the small boat docked at the shore, Seraphina untied it and climbed in, the oars clattering faintly as she pushed away from the pier. Rowing in her corset was an ordeal, each pull of the oars compressing her ribs and forcing her breath into shallow gasps. The frigid wind stung her cheeks, and her arms burned with the effort, but she pressed on, her eyes fixed on the distant shore.
By the time she landed, her breath came in ragged, wheezing gasps. She dragged the boat onto the rocky shore at a secluded spot far from the usual landing place, her legs trembling with exhaustion. But before she could take a single step, hands seized her from behind. She struggled, kicking and twisting, but her captors were prepared.
A rough hand stuffed a rag into her mouth, and a strip of cloth was tied tightly around her head to keep it in place. Her wrists were wrenched behind her back and bound with coarse rope, the fibers biting into her skin. A thick bag was pulled over her head, plunging her into darkness.
“Got her,” one of the men muttered, his voice gruff.
Without ceremony, she was hoisted back into the boat and rowed across the loch, her struggles futile against their strength.
Miss Blackthorn stood at the reformatory dock, rigid with fury as the boat approached. The girls whispered behind their hands, scandalized by the spectacle of a bound and gagged Seraphina being dragged ashore in full view of the Major and Elizabeth.
Once inside her office, Miss Blackthorn removed the bag from Seraphina’s head. Her anger was palpable, her cold demeanor more terrifying than an outburst. She stood before Seraphina, who had been unceremoniously dropped into a chair, her bindings and gag still in place.
“You dare cause such a scene,” Miss Blackthorn said icily, her voice low and controlled, “on a day when we have a visitor. Such behavior is beyond insubordination—it is an affront to this institution.”
Seraphina glared up at her, the defiance in her eyes undiminished despite her restraints. Miss Blackthorn leaned in closer, her expression one of restrained fury. “I see now that you require a lesson in humility, Miss Lockewood, one you will not soon forget.”
Miss Blackthorn’s icy glare remained fixed on Seraphina as she reached for a small silver bell on her desk and rang it sharply. The chime echoed through the office, crisp and commanding. Within moments, two maids entered—Morag, her sturdy frame and sharp Scottish tongue instantly recognizable, and the broad, stone-faced Russian maid, introduced only as Tatiana when Seraphina first arrived.
“Take her to the dressing room,” Miss Blackthorn ordered coldly. “We shall teach her the consequences of such disgraceful behavior.”
The maids curtsied before stepping forward. Seraphina, still bound and gagged, was hauled unceremoniously to her feet. They marched her down the hallway, their footsteps heavy against the stone floor. In the dressing room, a single lacing bar hung ominously from the ceiling.
Loch Thorne, “Dressing Room”# With practiced efficiency, Morag and Tatiana untied Seraphina’s wrists, though they kept the gag firmly in place. They removed her ruined clothing, peeling away the layers of her dress, underskirts, and corset until she stood in only her thin slip. Seraphina’s cheeks burned with humiliation, but her protests were muffled by the cloth in her mouth.
The maids guided her beneath the lacing bar and secured her wrists to it with thick leather straps. Tatiana turned the crank with slow precision, raising the bar until Seraphina’s arms were stretched above her head. The tension forced her to stand tall, her shoulders strained, and her balance wavered as they removed her shoes. When the bar was pulled even higher, her toes left the ground, and she was forced to balance precariously on tiptoe, her muscles trembling with effort.
From a wooden chest, Tatiana withdrew the punishment corset. It was an imposing garment of black leather, double-boned and reinforced with steel. Its length was alarming, covering the body from just above the knees to the base of the jaw, where an integrated neck corset curved upward like a dark, unyielding collar. It gleamed ominously in the lamplight, its multiple sets of laces and straps promising absolute restriction.
Working together, the maids slipped the corset around Seraphina’s body, pulling it into place and closing the heavy steel busk at the front. Even unfastened, the neck corset forced her head into an upright position, her chin lifted and her posture regal. The garment clung to her like a second skin, its weight pressing heavily against her frame.
Tatiana and Morag began tightening the primary laces around her torso. The pressure was immediate and overwhelming, forcing the air from Seraphina’s lungs in a sharp gasp. It felt like being caught in the crushing embrace of a bear; her ribs compressed, her waist narrowed, and her breath came in short, shallow bursts. The high, structured cups of the corset pushed her breasts upward, emphasizing her figure in a way that felt both stifling and deliberate.
They paused, stepping back to give her a moment of reprieve. Seraphina panted against the gag, her chest heaving as she tried to draw in air. But there was no escape from the unyielding pressure of the corset.
“Time for the boots,” Morag said grimly, retrieving a pair of black leather ballet boots from a nearby shelf. The shoes were monstrous, forcing the feet into an en-pointe position with impossibly high heels and stiffened shafts that extended up to the knees. Tatiana held Seraphina’s leg steady while Morag worked, sliding her foot into the first boot and pulling the laces taut. The leather encased her foot and lower leg completely, rigid at the ankle and holding her foot in perfect alignment with her shin. The second boot followed, laced with the same unyielding precision.
Once secured, the boots left her utterly dependent on the bar for balance. Her feet felt locked in place, the brutal arch of the heels forcing every muscle in her calves to strain with effort. The sensation was alien and excruciating, her toes bearing the full weight of her body with no hope of relief.
“She’ll not be strayin’ far in these,” Morag muttered, stepping back to survey their work.
Tatiana smirked faintly, her stern face betraying the smallest flicker of satisfaction. “Da,” she agreed, her accent heavy. “Now she learns.”
Seraphina’s breaths came quick and shallow, her body trembling under the combined weight of the corset and boots. Despite the pain and humiliation, her mind refused to yield.
The second round of lacing began with the same ruthless precision, but this time there was no hint of reprieve. Tatiana’s strong hands worked the laces of the corset’s primary section, pulling it tighter and tighter until Seraphina felt as though her torso had been carved from the leather itself. Her waist compressed further, the stays biting into her ribs with unrelenting force, and her breath became a shallow, staccato rhythm.
When Tatiana shifted to the lower lacing, Seraphina’s heart sank. Starting at the base of the corset, just below her hips, Tatiana pulled the laces upward, drawing the stiff leather around her thighs and knees. Each pull forced her knees closer together, eliminating any possibility of taking a normal step. The tension left her unable to bend her legs; she would be hobbled, forced to endure the unforgiving ballet boots and their merciless en-pointe position. Morag leaned in, tying the laces of the boots to the hem of the corset, securing them with a double knot that promised no release.
Seraphina gasped quietly against the gag, her balance increasingly precarious. Standing on her toes, her legs quivered with the effort of holding her weight, her calves burning as the strain intensified.
“Now fer the neck corset,” Morag muttered grimly, stepping back as Tatiana began pulling the upper laces with deliberate care. The integrated neck corset, which had already been snug, tightened further with each pass. The leather stretched her neck into an unnaturally upright position, forcing her chin slightly upward. The tension along her throat was immediate, but it was the upper edge of the corset that truly sealed her fate. The high seam pressed into her jawline, and any attempt to tilt or turn her head sent sharp, biting pokes into her skin.
Seraphina froze, her breaths shallow and quick. The realization dawned on her like a cold wave: she could not move her head, not even slightly, without pain. Speaking would be possible but excruciating, the upper rim of the neck corset promising to bite at her every word. Her throat burned as she tested it, murmuring a faint sound that cost her more than she had anticipated.
She swallowed hard, her mind racing. Miss Blackthorn would know. The woman would force her to speak, to answer in full, polite sentences as was required of a lady. And Seraphina would have no choice but to endure the pain, her voice soft and strained with every word.
The lacing bar descended slowly, releasing Seraphina’s arms and shoulders from their suspended tension. But the relief was fleeting. The moment her feet bore her full weight again, the excruciating pressure of the ballet boots made itself known. She wobbled precariously, her legs trembling as she fought to balance on the impossibly high heels. Morag and Tatiana steadied her on either side, their firm grips keeping her upright as she struggled against the pain radiating from her toes to her calves.
“Stand straight, lass,” Morag said, her tone brisk but not unkind. “The pain’s part o’ the lesson.”
Seraphina tried to adjust, the rigid neck corset preventing her from even glancing down to assess her footing. Her breaths came shallowly, the tight confines of the punishment corset compressing her ribs with every gasp. She stood stiffly, feeling trapped not only by the bindings but by her own body, betrayed by its limits.
Morag retrieved a pair of long, black leather gloves from a nearby table. They gleamed in the dim light, their structure suggesting they were far more than mere accessories. Tatiana held Seraphina steady, her iron grip unyielding, while Morag slid the gloves onto her arms.
The gloves reached past Seraphina’s elbows, ending just below her shoulders, where they were buttoned tightly and secured to the punishment corset. Their design was unforgiving; boning ran through the gloves, stiffening them so that Seraphina’s elbows could not bend. Worse still, additional rigid supports ran from the wrist to the fingers, locking her hands into a neutral, lifeless pose. Her fingers could not flex, her palms could not grip—her hands were rendered as useless as the carved wooden appendages of a marionette.
Tatiana removed the gag, pulling the rag from her mouth with the same efficiency she had displayed throughout the ordeal. Seraphina coughed softly, her throat sore from the pressure of the neck corset. Tatiana used the cloth to wipe away the spittle from her lips, her expression impassive as though this were no different from scrubbing a floor.
As the maids worked, the full extent of her bindings began to dawn on Seraphina. Her arms were rigid and useless, her hands decorative but inert. Her head was locked upright, the collar of the corset biting painfully at her jaw if she so much as thought of tilting it. Her torso was compressed and unyielding, and her legs, bound from knees to ankles, allowed only the smallest of steps. She could not sit, could not bend, could not raise her voice without sharp pain. And if she fell, she would be utterly helpless.
The finishing touches came swiftly. Morag and Tatiana dressed her in the reformatory’s standard uniform: petticoats, a stiff black woolen dress, and a pristine detachable white collar fastened snugly around her neck. Over her stiffened hands, they pulled a pair of regulation white gloves, completing the illusion of decorum. To finish her, her face was painted in the required makeup. Outwardly, she looked no different than any other young woman in the institution—proper, refined, every detail immaculate. But beneath the layers of fabric and propriety, Seraphina was almost entirely immobilized.
The maids finally fixed the bonnet to her head, buttoning it into place so that it aligned perfectly with the high collar of her corset. The snug straps around her chin left her head as rigid as ever, her limited field of vision reinforcing her inability to look down or to the side.
Tatiana stepped back, her critical eye assessing their work, while Morag gave a short nod of approval. “Right,” Morag said briskly. “Let’s take her tae Miss Blackthorn.”
Loch Thorne, “In Punishment”# With Morag on one side and Tatiana on the other, they led Seraphina from the dressing room. Her minuscule steps made the progress painfully slow, her knees locked too tightly together to allow for anything more than a shuffle. Each step sent another wave of pain from the ballet boots, her toes bearing her entire weight as she tottered forward.
Seraphina kept her head high—more from necessity than pride—her expression a mask of forced calm. Inside, her anger simmered, but her body’s limitations rendered her fury impotent. With every step closer to Miss Blackthorn, her resolve tightened like the stays of her corset. They could bind her, restrain her, and humiliate her, but they would not break her.
When Seraphina entered Miss Blackthorn’s office, her painfully careful steps and the slow shuffle of her toe-locked ballet boots announced her arrival as much as the creak of the door. Morag and Tatiana stood behind her, silent as sentinels, as she made her way to the center of the room. Miss Blackthorn looked up from her desk, her icy gaze sweeping over Seraphina with a faint hint of satisfaction. On the two chairs before the desk, the Major and Elizabeth Hartwell sat, their expressions markedly different—Elizabeth’s subdued and wary, the Major’s politely curious.
“Well,” Miss Blackthorn began, her tone glacial, “you certainly know how to make an impression, Miss Lockewood. The dear Major here wished to ensure that you returned safe and unharmed from your little excursion… with his boat.”
The Major rose to his full height, his military bearing evident in every line of his posture. He bowed slightly, his gaze fixed on Seraphina with polite interest. “Major Sebastian Hartwell, at your service,” he said formally. “And you, I presume, are Miss Lockewood.”
Seraphina knew better than to deviate from her role. With her head locked in position by the unrelenting neck corset, she could not lower her gaze, so she focused on presenting the perfect curtsy. The movement required shifting all her weight onto one toe, and the ballet boot bit cruelly into her arch as she dipped. Pain flared through her calf and foot, but her expression betrayed nothing.
The Major stepped forward and took her stiffened hand, his touch warm against the unyielding leather of her glove. He paused, his thumb brushing briefly over the boning embedded within. His eyes flicked downward, his brows rising in polite surprise, though his lips curled into an appreciative smile. “Exquisite,” he murmured, lifting her gloved hand to his lips and pressing a chaste kiss to the surface. He straightened, still smiling, and added, “Miss Lockewood, your posture and figure are nothing short of immaculate. I trust you are none the worse for wear after your… adventure.”
Seraphina smiled as sweetly as her situation allowed, her lips curving in a polite yet empty expression. Her jaw ached from the pressure of the collar, and every word came at the cost of sharp jabs from the upper rim of the neck corset. “You are most kind, Major Hartwell,” she replied, her voice soft and measured. “I assure you, I am quite well. The Major’s gaze lingered on her face, his sharp blue eyes catching the faintest tension at the corners of her mouth. He seemed to notice the collar for the first time, its edge pressing cruelly against her jawline and holding her head in its rigid, regal position. His smile deepened, his admiration evident. “Such discipline,” he remarked, almost to himself. “It is rare to see such grace and countenance maintained under what must be extraordinary… demands.”
Seraphina’s smile tightened. “I endeavor to meet the expectations placed upon me,” she replied, her tone still polite but edged with the faintest strain.
“An admirable quality, Miss Lockewood,” the Major said warmly. “One that reflects most favorably upon you.”
Miss Blackthorn’s sharp voice cut through the moment. “Indeed,” she said, her tone cool. “Miss Lockewood’s education here is rigorous, but such standards are necessary to produce results.”
The Major inclined his head toward Miss Blackthorn. “I can see that the results are exceptional, Miss Blackthorn. Miss Blackthorn turned her gaze to Seraphina, her tone cool but edged with a faint undercurrent of triumph. “Thank you for your poise, Miss Lockewood. You may return to your duties.”

With their steadying hands on her arms, they began guiding her out of the room, her minuscule steps slow and faltering. Seraphina’s posture remained perfect—rigidly upright and unyielding—but her thoughts churned with anger and frustration as she was led back to class.
The punishment corset revealed its full cruelty as the hours dragged on. Every aspect of it was designed to enforce relentless, breathless elegance. The shoulder straps, fastened behind her back, pulled her shoulders down and back, forcing her chest forward and exaggerating her already emphasized posture. The pressure on her ribs and abdomen never relented, making each breath a shallow, gasping effort.
The neck corset was the crowning indignity. Its high collar locked her head in a fixed, regal position, rendering her unable to turn or tilt her head. She couldn’t look down to see where her feet were stepping, couldn’t glance at her hands when they rested uselessly in front of her, frozen in their stiffened gloves. Even speaking was an ordeal—the high edge of the collar bit sharply into her skin whenever she tried to form words, and the restricted airflow made her voice faint and strained.
Sitting was impossible. The lower lacing of the corset, cinched tightly from her bum to her knees, held her legs in an unbending line. The ballet boots forced her to balance on her toes, their punishing design ensuring that every step sent searing pain through her feet and calves. Relief was a distant, unattainable dream. She was utterly at the mercy of the corset and boots, locked into an elegant torment that allowed for no escape.
Her hands were equally useless. The rigid boning in her gloves immobilized her fingers and wrists, leaving her unable to grip or manipulate anything. She couldn’t lift, carry, or even steady herself if she stumbled. Her hands were purely decorative now—mute symbols of submission, stripped of utility.
The realization came slowly and cruelly: all she could do was stand, posed and poised, silent and helpless.
Her dependence on Morag grew rapidly. The robust maid became her only lifeline, guiding her through the day with brusque efficiency. Morag fed her spoonfuls of food, held cups of water to her lips, and led her from one place to another with a steady hand on her arm. Seraphina hated it—the indignity of being treated like a child, reliant on someone else for every basic necessity.
Free time, once an escape to the garden or the library, became another humiliation. With no means to move independently, Seraphina was placed in a corner of her room, her neck tethered to a wardrobe hook by a short chain. The tether forced her to remain upright, staring at the blank walls. The sense of helplessness was overwhelming. She couldn’t turn her head, couldn’t shift her posture, couldn’t even look down to distract herself. She was as immobilized as a doll stored between play.
The chain at her neck felt like a leash, a humiliating symbol of her complete subjugation. The isolation of the corner magnified the humiliation, leaving her alone with her thoughts, trapped in her binding and her own mind. Her back ached, her feet throbbed, and every shallow breath reminded her of the corset’s crushing embrace.
“How long?” she wondered silently, her eyes fixed on the unyielding corner. “How long does Miss Blackthorn intend to keep me like this? Can I endure?”
The hours stretched endlessly, her helplessness gnawing at her pride. For now, all Seraphina could do was endure, waiting for an opportunity, for some crack in the unrelenting facade of the reformatory’s control. Until then, she remained locked in her bindings, staring at the corner, her anger burning like a cold, steady flame.
Night fell, and with it came the now-familiar ritual of preparation. Morag’s presence was both a relief and a dread. Relief, because she would remove the punishment corset that had tortured Seraphina’s body all day. Dread, because what awaited was another layer of confinement, one that offered no reprieve.
As the last laces of the punishment corset were undone, Seraphina exhaled a shallow breath, her torso aching from the strain. Morag worked quickly, lacing her into her standard night corset, which extended from her knees to her chest. It was looser than the day corset but still far from comfortable, its boning ensuring she remained upright and restrained.
Next came the leather mittens, encasing her hands and fingers, curling them into useless balls. Morag buckled the straps tightly, ensuring they would not slip, and checked the bindings at Seraphina’s wrists. Then, wordlessly, she guided Seraphina to the bed.
Laid out on the bed was the leather cocoon, its polished surface gleaming faintly in the dim lamplight. It was an all-encompassing garment, lined with stiff boning and reinforced seams. Morag helped Seraphina lie down, the maid’s practiced efficiency leaving no room for hesitation. The cocoon was drawn up around her, layer by layer, the laces pulled tightly to compress her body further into its confines. The integrated hood enclosed her head completely, silencing her as the final ties were secured.
Seraphina lay in complete stillness. The leather pressed against her skin from every angle, its unyielding embrace immobilizing her entirely. Her arms, pinned at her sides, couldn’t so much as twitch. Her legs, locked in place by the stiffened lower section, were as unmovable as if they were bound with iron. The hood muffled every sound, even her own breathing, until the silence was so profound it felt like a weight pressing against her ears.
At first, her mind turned to escape. She envisioned breaking free, tearing through the bindings, seizing revenge on Miss Blackthorn and the maids who had participated in her subjugation. The images were vivid and detailed—her hands breaking through the mittens, a knife slicing through the leather, her body free and strong again.
But the silence, the stillness, began to warp her thoughts. Without sensation or movement to anchor her, her mind drifted. The visions of revenge blurred and softened, replaced by images of submission. Of kneeling before Miss Blackthorn, her voice soft and compliant, her posture perfect. She saw herself curtsying, smiling with genuine warmth, thanking the woman for her discipline.
Then, unexpectedly, the dreams took another turn. The Major’s face appeared, vivid and commanding. She saw his piercing blue eyes, his polite smile, the way he had admired her composure. The image of him kissing her gloved hand lingered, morphing into something far more intimate. She imagined his hands, strong and steady, removing her gloves, his voice low and warm, praising her for her obedience. The dreams became heated, adult, arousing—emotions she had never felt with such intensity before.
Her body responded instinctively, but the cocoon held her utterly still. Her mittens, pinned to her sides, prevented her hands from moving. The tightness of the leather, the compression of the corset, the immobility of her legs—all conspired to deny her even the smallest physical reaction. The sensations built in her mind but remained locked within, unattainable, leaving her trapped between the dream and the unyielding reality of her bindings.
Time ceased to have meaning. Awake, asleep, dreaming, hallucinating—it all blurred together in the sensory deprivation. Her breaths were shallow and steady, her thoughts circling endlessly through escape, submission, and desire. The Major’s face haunted her, a new and unexpected obsession taking root in the depths of her mind.
Loch Thorne, “A Week in Punishment”# The week dragged on with merciless monotony, each day and night blending into a continuum of agony and deprivation. Seraphina remained locked in her punishment corset and ballet boots, her every breath constrained, her every movement a study in pain. The corset’s relentless embrace crushed her ribs and compressed her lungs, leaving her perpetually breathless. The high collar bit into her jawline, forbidding her the slightest tilt or turn of her head, while the stiffened gloves rendered her hands little more than decorative appendages. She was trapped, not only by her bindings but by the unyielding monotony of her circumstances.
The nights were worse. Encased in the leather cocoon, silenced and immobilized, she drifted in and out of fitful dreams and hallucinatory visions. The sensory deprivation twisted her thoughts, blurring the line between reality and imagination. The Major’s face haunted her still, but now his visage mingled with shadowy images of escape and revenge. She plotted endlessly, her mind a battlefield of defiance that refused to yield.
The human mind, fragile yet indomitable, has a way of adapting to even the most grueling conditions. For Seraphina, the pain and humiliation did not break her spirit; instead, they forged it into something sharper, harder, and infinitely more dangerous. Her emotional spectrum narrowed as the days wore on. Joy, fear, love, and hope—these emotions dissolved like mist in the face of her unrelenting reality. What remained was a distilled clarity: patience and vengeance.
Outwardly, Seraphina became the perfect vision of a broken Victorian lady. Her curtsies were graceful, her posture immaculate, her demeanor meek and compliant. She murmured thanks when corrected, curtsied when praised, and held her poise with the elegance of a doll. But behind the mask of submission, her mind worked tirelessly.
Pain, once her tormentor, became background noise. It was always there, gnawing at her ribs, her calves, her throat, but she learned to push it aside, to focus on the engine of cold hatred that drove her forward. Every moment of suffering sharpened her resolve. The deprivation, the humiliation, the complete helplessness—all of it became fuel for her plans.
She thought of Edmond Dantès, the Count of Monte Cristo, the prisoner who endured years of imprisonment only to rise as an avenger with meticulous precision. Seraphina replayed her own revenge in excruciating detail, refining it with every passing hour. Every humiliation she endured became a step in her mental preparation, every moment of helplessness a catalyst for her eventual retaliation.
Miss Blackthorn and the staff began to believe they had succeeded. Seraphina’s outward behavior was flawless; she appeared every bit the obedient ward. But Miss Blackthorn remained uneasy. There was no breaking point, no sobbing capitulation, no outward sign of surrender. Seraphina was too quiet, too composed. It was as though she had moved beyond resistance into something darker, something colder.
And that was exactly what Seraphina wanted them to think.
The deprivation had honed her hatred into a tool, stripped of impulsive emotion and refined into methodical intent. She didn’t lash out, didn’t waste her energy on futile resistance. She waited, patient as a predator in the shadows, biding her time until the moment came when her captors would falter.
The transformation was complete. Seraphina Lockewood, the rebellious girl who had once roamed the jungles of India, was gone. In her place stood a woman forged in the fires of suffering, her hatred a weapon, her patience unyielding. And when the time came, she would not hesitate. She would make them pay. All of them.
The week finally ended, and with it, Seraphina’s time in the punishment corset and its cruel accompaniments. Miss Blackthorn’s decision to relent was not made lightly. She sat in her office, gazing out the window at the gray Scottish sky, her fingers drumming lightly on the polished wood of her desk. Her own memories resurfaced unbidden—she, too, had once stood in the rigid torment of such bindings, albeit only for a day. She remembered the unrelenting pressure of the corset, the agonizing bite of the neck collar, and the maddening helplessness of immobilized limbs. It had left her trembling and tearful by nightfall. One day had been enough to carve a deep understanding of its severity. Seraphina had endured a week.
With a curt command, Miss Blackthorn ordered Morag and Tatiana to return Seraphina to her regular uniform. The maids moved efficiently, unlacing her from the punishment corset and peeling away its layers. When they guided her back into the familiar slip, corset, and woolen school dress, Seraphina showed no outward reaction, though the regular uniform now felt like a mere annoyance rather than the prison it once had been.
The days resumed their monotonous routine, but Seraphina moved through them with effortless grace. She followed every rule of the reformatory, curtsied at the right moments, spoke only when spoken to, and maintained perfect posture. Her instructors praised her as an exemplary student, a model of Victorian refinement. But behind the polite smile and perfect manners, her resolve simmered quietly, waiting.
As the months passed and the year drew to a close, anticipation grew among the girls at Loch Thorne. The grand ball, the pinnacle of their reformatory experience, approached with the promise of glimmering chandeliers, elegant waltzes, and the possibility to charm future husbands. Seraphina, like her peers, felt the excitement thrumming beneath the surface. However, while others dreamed of dazzling ballrooms and whispered of potential suitors, her mind was fixed on other plans.
The preparation for the ball was rigorous, each day a medley of lessons designed to mold the girls into paragons of Victorian womanhood. Waist-training was a constant presence, the corsets cinching ever tighter, their stays reminding the girls of the posture and poise expected of them. But there was more to their training than the physical constraints of their attire. The girls learned to dance, flirt, and conduct themselves with the grace befitting ladies of society.
Deportment classes with Miss Blackthorn herself were a study in discipline. Her presence alone was enough to silence the room, her eyes scanning for the slightest deviation in posture. She demanded the girls stand tall, their spines straight and their chins held high. Slouching, what little their uniforms allowed, was met with a swift correction, her voice unyielding as she reminded them of the virtues of dignity and elegance. Under her watchful gaze, the girls learned to move with a fluid grace.
In dance class, Mr. Grayson’s quick temper and punctilious nature drove the girls to perfect their steps. His cane tapped rhythmically on the floor, a metronome guiding their movements as they practiced the waltz, the quadrille, and other dances. With only themselves as partners, the girls learned to perform their moves, their skirts swishing in time with the music.
Etiquette lessons with Mrs. Everstone were equally exacting. The widowed vicar’s wife took delight in pointing out infractions, her remarks cutting through the room like a knife. The girls learned the nuances of social interaction, from the proper way to hold a teacup to the delicate art of conversation. Every curtsey, every nod was scrutinized, the girls striving for the seamless elegance expected of them.
Mademoiselle Vivienne Artois presided over conversation classes in English and French, her standards as high as her patience was short. Enunciation had to be perfect, grammar flawless. Her disdain for errors and her sharp tongue were a constajt a reminder that words carried weight and power. Under her tutelage, the girls learned to speak with sophistication.
Through it all, Seraphina outwardly joined in the enthusiasm of her peers, discussing gowns and dances with the same demure excitement. She mastered the art of the coy smile, the flirtatious glance, all while her mind remained firmly on her own objectives. As the ball approached, she felt the weight of expectation, of the roles they were preparing to play, but her resolve remained untouched. The grand ball would be a culmination of her time at the reformatory, but for Seraphina, it was merely a step in her own carefully laid plans.

From there, they boarded a train bound for the capital, their presence drawing stares and murmurs from fellow passengers. She glanced at herself in the mirror, noting how the Indian-inspired details set her apart from the other girls. For a moment, her lips curved into a faint smile—not of pride, but of satisfaction.
